# Page: Interactive Mode (Jupyter/Colab)

# Interactive Mode (Jupyter/Colab)

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [Docs/UserManual.md](Docs/UserManual.md)
- [config.yaml](config.yaml)
- [run](run)
- [submit](submit)

</details>



This page describes BioPipelines' interactive execution mode for Jupyter notebooks and Google Colab environments. Interactive mode enables on-the-fly execution where tools run immediately upon instantiation, allowing step-by-step development and real-time feedback. This differs from cluster execution ([4.1](#4.1)) and local execution ([4.2](#4.2)), which use a two-phase model.

For information about the two-phase execution model used in cluster and local modes, see [Pipeline Context and Resources](#3.1) and [Tools and BaseConfig](#3.2).

---

## Automatic Environment Detection

BioPipelines automatically detects when running in Jupyter/Colab environments and activates interactive mode without requiring explicit configuration. The detection mechanism examines the Python runtime context and loads appropriate configuration files.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    Start["Python interpreter starts"]
    CheckIPython["Check for IPython kernel"]
    CheckColab["Check for google.colab module"]
    LoadConfig["Load config file"]
    
    ConfigYAML["Load config.yaml<br/>(cluster/local)"]
    ColabYAML["Load colab.yaml<br/>(notebook)"]
    
    SetEnvManager["Set env_manager"]
    Conda["env_manager: 'mamba'/'conda'"]
    Pip["env_manager: 'pip'"]
    
    SetExecutionMode["Set execution mode"]
    TwoPhase["Two-phase execution<br/>(generate + submit/run)"]
    OnTheFly["On-the-fly execution<br/>(immediate execution)"]
    
    Start --> CheckIPython
    CheckIPython -->|"IPython.get_ipython() exists"| CheckColab
    CheckIPython -->|"Not in IPython"| LoadConfig
    
    CheckColab -->|"google.colab available"| ColabYAML
    CheckColab -->|"Standard Jupyter"| ColabYAML
    LoadConfig -->|"Standard Python"| ConfigYAML
    
    ConfigYAML --> SetEnvManager
    ColabYAML --> SetEnvManager
    
    SetEnvManager --> Conda
    SetEnvManager --> Pip
    
    Conda --> TwoPhase
    Pip --> OnTheFly
    
    TwoPhase --> SetExecutionMode
    OnTheFly --> SetExecutionMode
```

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:73-139](), [config.yaml:1-188]()

The detection flow prioritizes `colab.yaml` when in notebook environments, which sets `env_manager: "pip"` and automatically enables on-the-fly execution. In standard Python environments, `config.yaml` is loaded with `env_manager: "mamba"` or `"conda"`, defaulting to two-phase execution.

---

## Configuration File Comparison

Interactive mode uses a separate configuration file (`colab.yaml`) that overrides key settings from the standard `config.yaml`:

| Setting | config.yaml (Cluster) | colab.yaml (Notebooks) |
|---------|----------------------|------------------------|
| `env_manager` | `"mamba"` or `"conda"` | `"pip"` |
| Output directory | Configured path (e.g., `<user>/BioPipelines`) | `./BioPipelines/` (current directory) |
| SLURM modules | Required for cluster | Ignored |
| Container support | Singularity/Apptainer paths | Not applicable |
| Environment mapping | Tool → conda environment | Tool → pip package |

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:127-136](), [config.yaml:62-163]()

The `env_manager: "pip"` setting transforms environment activation into no-ops, as all tools share the single Python environment provided by Jupyter/Colab. Tool-specific conda environments defined in `config.yaml` are replaced by pip-based installation commands.

---

## On-the-Fly Execution Model

On-the-fly execution fundamentally changes when tool logic executes. In cluster/local modes, tool instantiation only generates bash scripts (configuration phase), with execution deferred to SLURM or sequential bash execution. In interactive mode, tool instantiation triggers immediate execution.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as "Notebook Cell"
    participant Pipeline as "Pipeline Context"
    participant Tool as "Tool Instance<br/>(e.g., RFdiffusion)"
    participant HelpScript as "Helper Script<br/>(e.g., pipe_rfdiffusion.py)"
    participant Filesystem as "Filesystem"
    
    User->>Pipeline: Pipeline("Project", "Job")
    Note over Pipeline: Context remains active<br/>across cells
    
    User->>Tool: tool = RFdiffusion(...)
    Tool->>Tool: validate_params()
    Tool->>Tool: predict output IDs
    Tool->>Pipeline: auto-register
    
    Tool->>Tool: configure_inputs()
    Tool->>Tool: generate_script()
    Tool->>Filesystem: Write config JSON
    Tool->>Filesystem: Write bash script
    
    Note over Tool,HelpScript: IMMEDIATE EXECUTION
    Tool->>HelpScript: bash <tool>.sh
    
    HelpScript->>Filesystem: Read config JSON
    HelpScript->>HelpScript: Execute tool logic
    HelpScript->>Filesystem: Write outputs to<br/>./BioPipelines/.../001_Tool/
    HelpScript->>Filesystem: Create .completion marker
    
    HelpScript-->>Tool: Exit with code 0
    Tool-->>User: Return StandardizedOutput<br/>(tool results available)
    
    Note over User: Next cell can use<br/>tool.streams.structures
```

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:421-454]()

### Key Behavioral Differences

Interactive mode introduces several execution model changes:

| Aspect | Cluster/Local Mode | Interactive Mode |
|--------|-------------------|------------------|
| **`with` statement** | Required to define pipeline scope | Optional; pipeline persists across cells |
| **Tool execution** | Deferred to bash script submission | Immediate upon instantiation |
| **Output availability** | After SLURM job completes | After cell execution completes |
| **Execution order** | Controlled by batch dependencies | Sequential, cell-by-cell |
| **stdout/stderr** | Written to log files | Streamed to notebook output |
| **Resources()** | Controls SLURM allocation | Parsed but ignored for execution |
| **Completion checking** | Prevents duplicate SLURM jobs | Skips already-completed steps on re-run |

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:445-454]()

The optional `with` statement allows pipelines to span multiple notebook cells, supporting iterative development:

```python
# Cell 1: Initialize pipeline (optional with statement)
Pipeline("Examples", "interactive_design",
         description="Iterative binder design")

lysozyme = PDB("168L")
rfd = RFdiffusion(pdb=lysozyme, contigs='50-70/A81-140', num_designs=3)
# rfd.streams.structures is immediately available

# Cell 2: Continue in same pipeline
pmpnn = ProteinMPNN(structures=rfd, num_sequences=2)
# pmpnn.streams.sequences is immediately available

# Cell 3: Analyze results and add more tools
from biopipelines.panda import Panda
best = Panda(tables=pmpnn.tables.sequences,
             operations=[Panda.sort("score", ascending=False)])
```

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:426-441]()

---

## Pipeline Lifecycle in Notebooks

The `Pipeline` context manager exhibits different lifecycle semantics in interactive mode compared to standard Python execution.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Inactive
    
    Inactive --> Active: Pipeline() called
    Active --> Active: Tool instantiation<br/>(executes immediately)
    Active --> Inactive: Re-run Pipeline() cell
    Active --> Active: Continue across cells
    
    note right of Active
        Pipeline context persists
        across notebook cells
        until Pipeline() is
        re-instantiated
    end note
    
    note right of Inactive
        New Pipeline() call
        starts fresh context
        with new job directory
    end note
```

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:421-454]()

### Multi-Cell Pipeline Pattern

```python
# Cell 1: Create pipeline
Pipeline("Examples", "test", description="Multi-step workflow")
proteins = PDB(["4ufc", "1aki"])

# Cell 2: Add tools (pipeline still active)
rfd = RFdiffusion(pdb=proteins, contigs='50-100', num_designs=2)

# Cell 3: Continue adding tools
pmpnn = ProteinMPNN(structures=rfd, num_sequences=3)

# Cell 4: Analyze
print(f"Generated {len(pmpnn.streams.sequences)} sequences")
print(pmpnn.streams.sequences.ids)

# Cell 5: Re-run Pipeline() to start fresh
Pipeline("Examples", "test_v2", description="Second iteration")
# Previous pipeline is no longer active
```

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:426-441]()

Re-running the cell containing `Pipeline()` instantiation creates a new pipeline context with a new job directory. Previous pipeline outputs remain on disk but are no longer the active context.

---

## Environment Management with pip

Interactive mode replaces conda/mamba environment management with pip-based installation. Each tool's `install()` method executes `pip install` commands instead of creating isolated conda environments.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph ClusterMode["Cluster Mode (config.yaml)"]
        ClusterEnv["env_manager: 'mamba'"]
        EnvMap["environments:<br/>RFdiffusion → SE3nv<br/>ProteinMPNN → SE3nv<br/>Boltz2 → Boltz2Env"]
        CondaEnvs["Isolated conda<br/>environments"]
        
        ClusterEnv --> EnvMap
        EnvMap --> CondaEnvs
    end
    
    subgraph InteractiveMode["Interactive Mode (colab.yaml)"]
        InteractiveEnv["env_manager: 'pip'"]
        SingleEnv["Single Python<br/>environment<br/>(Jupyter/Colab)"]
        PipInstall["pip install commands"]
        
        InteractiveEnv --> SingleEnv
        SingleEnv --> PipInstall
    end
    
    style ClusterMode fill:#f9f9f9
    style InteractiveMode fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:88-93](), [config.yaml:62-163]()

### Environment Activation Behavior

When `env_manager: "pip"`, environment activation commands become no-ops:

| Operation | Cluster Mode | Interactive Mode |
|-----------|--------------|------------------|
| Tool instantiation | Records environment name from `config.yaml` | Ignores environment mapping |
| Script generation | Writes `mamba activate <env>` to bash scripts | Writes no-op or skips activation |
| Execution | Activates tool-specific conda environment | Uses current Jupyter kernel |
| Dependencies | Isolated per-tool environments | Shared across all tools |
| Conflicts | Prevented by isolation | User must manage manually |

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:88-93](), [config.yaml:140-142]()

---

## Tool Installation

Tools must be explicitly installed in interactive mode using the `.install()` class method. This replaces the pre-configured conda environments used in cluster mode.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as "Notebook Cell"
    participant Pipeline as "Pipeline Context"
    participant ToolClass as "Tool Class<br/>(e.g., RFdiffusion)"
    participant GitRepo as "Git Repository"
    participant Pip as "pip installer"
    participant Filesystem as "Filesystem"
    
    User->>Pipeline: with Pipeline("Setup", "install"):
    User->>ToolClass: ToolClass.install()
    
    ToolClass->>Filesystem: Check if already installed
    
    alt Not installed
        ToolClass->>GitRepo: git clone <repo_url>
        GitRepo-->>Filesystem: Clone to ./data/ToolName/
        
        ToolClass->>Pip: pip install -e ./data/ToolName/
        Pip-->>ToolClass: Installation complete
        
        ToolClass->>Filesystem: Write .install_complete marker
    else Already installed
        ToolClass->>User: Skip (marker exists)
    end
    
    ToolClass-->>User: Installation ready
```

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:94-108]()

### Installation Example

```python
from biopipelines.pipeline import Pipeline
from biopipelines.rfdiffusion import RFdiffusion
from biopipelines.protein_mpnn import ProteinMPNN
from biopipelines.alphafold import AlphaFold

# Dedicated installation pipeline
with Pipeline("Setup", "install", description="Install tools"):
    RFdiffusion.install()
    ProteinMPNN.install()
    AlphaFold.install()
    # Each .install() runs once per session
    # Re-running the cell skips already-completed installations
```

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:98-108]()

Installation commands clone repositories to `./data/<ToolName>/` and execute `pip install -e .` in the repository directory. Completion markers prevent duplicate installations when cells are re-run.

---

## Output Directory Structure

Interactive mode writes outputs to the current working directory instead of the configured shared storage path:

```
./BioPipelines/
├── <project>/
│   └── <job>_001/
│       ├── RunTime/
│       │   ├── pipeline.sh
│       │   ├── 001_RFdiffusion.sh
│       │   └── 002_ProteinMPNN.sh
│       ├── Logs/
│       │   ├── 001_RFdiffusion.log
│       │   └── 002_ProteinMPNN.log
│       ├── ToolOutputs/
│       │   ├── 001_RFdiffusion.json
│       │   └── 002_ProteinMPNN.json
│       └── 001_RFdiffusion/
│           ├── .completion
│           ├── .expected_outputs.json
│           └── output_files...
```

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:132-134](), [Docs/UserManual.md:556-577]()

The `local_output=True` flag is automatically set when `on_the_fly` is enabled, overriding the `biopipelines_output` path from `config.yaml`. This ensures notebook outputs remain in the working directory for easy access.

---

## Execution Flow Comparison

The following diagram contrasts the execution flows between cluster mode (two-phase) and interactive mode (on-the-fly):

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph ClusterMode["Cluster Mode (submit script)"]
        C1["Pipeline script:<br/>with Pipeline():<br/>  tool1 = Tool1()<br/>  tool2 = Tool2()"]
        C2["Configuration Phase:<br/>Generate bash scripts<br/>Predict outputs<br/>Write configs"]
        C3["Exit Python:<br/>Output RunTime paths"]
        C4["Submit script:<br/>Parse RunTime/<br/>Submit to SLURM"]
        C5["Execution Phase:<br/>SLURM executes<br/>bash scripts<br/>(async)"]
        
        C1 --> C2
        C2 --> C3
        C3 --> C4
        C4 --> C5
    end
    
    subgraph InteractiveMode["Interactive Mode (Jupyter/Colab)"]
        I1["Notebook cell:<br/>Pipeline()"]
        I2["Notebook cell:<br/>tool1 = Tool1()"]
        I3["Generate config<br/>Generate script"]
        I4["Execute bash script<br/>(blocking)"]
        I5["tool1 outputs available"]
        I6["Notebook cell:<br/>tool2 = Tool2(tool1)"]
        I7["Generate config<br/>Generate script"]
        I8["Execute bash script<br/>(blocking)"]
        I9["tool2 outputs available"]
        
        I1 --> I2
        I2 --> I3
        I3 --> I4
        I4 --> I5
        I5 --> I6
        I6 --> I7
        I7 --> I8
        I8 --> I9
    end
    
    style ClusterMode fill:#f9f9f9
    style InteractiveMode fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:162-171](), [Docs/UserManual.md:421-454]()

In cluster mode, the entire pipeline is configured before any execution occurs. In interactive mode, each tool executes immediately upon instantiation, enabling incremental development and immediate result inspection.

---

## Google Colab Specific Considerations

Google Colab imposes runtime constraints that affect interactive mode:

### Session Ephemerality

Colab sessions disconnect after inactivity periods or runtime limits. All installed tools and generated outputs are lost upon disconnection. Mitigation strategies:

```python
# Mount Google Drive for persistent storage
from google.colab import drive
drive.mount('/content/drive')

# Run pipeline with outputs to Drive
Pipeline("Examples", "design", 
         description="Persistent outputs",
         local_output=True)  # Still writes to ./BioPipelines/

# Manually copy critical outputs
!cp -r ./BioPipelines/Examples/design_001/001_Boltz2/ /content/drive/MyDrive/results/
```

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:137-139]()

### GPU Allocation

Colab assigns GPU types dynamically. The `Resources()` call is parsed but does not control GPU allocation:

```python
# This is parsed but does not affect Colab GPU assignment
Resources(gpu="A100", memory="32GB")  

# Use the GPU Colab provides
import torch
print(f"GPU: {torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)}")
print(f"Memory: {torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory / 1e9:.1f} GB")
```

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:127-136]()

### Installation Persistence

Tool installations persist for the session duration but must be re-run after runtime disconnects:

```python
# Cell 1: Always run first (idempotent due to completion markers)
!git clone https://github.com/locbp-uzh/biopipelines
%cd biopipelines
!pip install -e .

# Cell 2: Install tools (skips if already done this session)
with Pipeline("Setup", "install"):
    RFdiffusion.install()
    ProteinMPNN.install()
```

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:79-108]()

---

## Completion Checking and Re-runs

Interactive mode preserves BioPipelines' completion checking mechanism. Tools inspect the filesystem for `.completion` markers before executing:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    Start["Tool instantiation"]
    CheckCompletion["Check for<br/>.completion marker"]
    ExpectedOutputs["Read<br/>.expected_outputs.json"]
    VerifyFiles["Verify all expected<br/>files exist"]
    
    Execute["Execute helper script"]
    WriteOutputs["Write outputs"]
    WriteCompletion["Write .completion marker"]
    
    LoadOutputs["Load outputs from disk"]
    ReturnTool["Return StandardizedOutput"]
    
    Start --> CheckCompletion
    CheckCompletion -->|"Marker exists"| ExpectedOutputs
    CheckCompletion -->|"Marker missing"| Execute
    
    ExpectedOutputs --> VerifyFiles
    VerifyFiles -->|"All files exist"| LoadOutputs
    VerifyFiles -->|"Files missing"| Execute
    
    Execute --> WriteOutputs
    WriteOutputs --> WriteCompletion
    WriteCompletion --> ReturnTool
    
    LoadOutputs --> ReturnTool
```

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:452-453]()

This enables safe re-execution of notebook cells:

```python
# First run: Executes all tools
rfd = RFdiffusion(pdb=lysozyme, contigs='50-100', num_designs=5)
pmpnn = ProteinMPNN(structures=rfd, num_sequences=3)

# Re-run same cell: Skips completed tools, loads from disk
rfd = RFdiffusion(pdb=lysozyme, contigs='50-100', num_designs=5)  # Skipped
pmpnn = ProteinMPNN(structures=rfd, num_sequences=3)  # Skipped
```

To force re-execution, delete the `.completion` marker:

```python
import os
completion_marker = "./BioPipelines/Examples/test_001/001_RFdiffusion/.completion"
if os.path.exists(completion_marker):
    os.remove(completion_marker)
```

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:452-453]()

---

## Forcing Interactive Mode Outside Notebooks

Interactive mode can be explicitly enabled in standard Python scripts using the `on_the_fly` parameter:

```python
from biopipelines.pipeline import Pipeline

# Force on-the-fly execution in a .py script
with Pipeline("Test", "local_dev", 
              description="Local development",
              on_the_fly=True):
    
    lysozyme = PDB("168L")
    rfd = RFdiffusion(pdb=lysozyme, contigs='50-100', num_designs=3)
    # Blocks until RFdiffusion completes
    
    pmpnn = ProteinMPNN(structures=rfd, num_sequences=2)
    # Blocks until ProteinMPNN completes
```

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:443-444]()

This is useful for rapid prototyping without SLURM overhead, though cluster/local execution modes are recommended for production workflows.

---

## Limitations and Workarounds

### No Batch Dependencies

Interactive mode executes tools sequentially in cell order. The `Resources()` batch dependency mechanism is ignored:

```python
# In cluster mode, this creates two SLURM batches with dependencies
Resources(gpu="V100", time="4:00:00")  # Batch 1
tool1 = RFdiffusion(...)

Resources(time="2:00:00")  # Batch 2 (waits for Batch 1)
tool2 = Panda(...)

# In interactive mode, both Resources() calls are no-ops
# Tools execute sequentially regardless
```

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:447-448]()

### No Parallel Execution

All tools execute sequentially in interactive mode. For parallel execution, use cluster mode with SLURM array jobs.

### Resource Constraints

Interactive environments have fixed resource allocations:
- **Colab Free:** ~12-16 GB RAM, T4 GPU (16 GB VRAM)
- **Colab Pro:** ~25-30 GB RAM, V100/A100 GPU
- **Jupyter local:** Host machine resources

Large-scale workflows may require cluster execution ([4.1](#4.1)).

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:132-134]()

---

## Complete Colab Example

```python
# Cell 1: Setup (run once per session)
!git clone https://github.com/locbp-uzh/biopipelines
%cd biopipelines
!pip install -e .

# Cell 2: Install tools
from biopipelines.pipeline import Pipeline
from biopipelines.rfdiffusion import RFdiffusion
from biopipelines.protein_mpnn import ProteinMPNN
from biopipelines.alphafold import AlphaFold

with Pipeline("Setup", "install", description="Install tools"):
    RFdiffusion.install()
    ProteinMPNN.install()
    AlphaFold.install()

# Cell 3: Run workflow
from biopipelines.entities import PDB

Pipeline("Examples", "binder_design",
         description="RFdiffusion → ProteinMPNN → AlphaFold")

target = PDB("168L")
backbones = RFdiffusion(pdb=target, 
                        contigs='50-70/A81-140',
                        num_designs=5)
# backbones.streams.structures immediately available

sequences = ProteinMPNN(structures=backbones, 
                        num_sequences=3)
# sequences.streams.sequences immediately available

predictions = AlphaFold(proteins=sequences)
# predictions.streams.structures immediately available

# Cell 4: Analyze results
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv(predictions.tables.confidence.info.path)
print(df.head())
print(f"Generated {len(predictions.streams.structures)} predictions")

# Cell 5: Filter and visualize
from biopipelines.panda import Panda
from biopipelines.pymol_tool import PyMOL

best = Panda(
    tables=predictions.tables.confidence,
    operations=[Panda.sort("plddt", ascending=False), Panda.head(3)],
    pool=predictions
)

pymol = PyMOL(
    structures=best.streams.structures,
    commands=["zoom", "show cartoon", "color spectrum"]
)
```

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:79-124](), [Docs/UserManual.md:426-441]()

---

## Summary: Interactive vs. Cluster/Local

| Feature | Cluster Mode ([4.1](#4.1)) | Local Mode ([4.2](#4.2)) | Interactive Mode |
|---------|---------------------------|-------------------------|------------------|
| **Execution model** | Two-phase (generate + SLURM) | Two-phase (generate + bash) | On-the-fly (immediate) |
| **Environment** | conda/mamba per tool | conda/mamba per tool | Single pip environment |
| **Pipeline scope** | `with` statement required | `with` statement required | `with` optional, spans cells |
| **Tool execution** | Async via SLURM | Sequential bash scripts | Sequential, blocking |
| **Output location** | Configured in `config.yaml` | Configured in `config.yaml` | `./BioPipelines/` |
| **Resources()** | Controls SLURM allocation | Ignored | Parsed but ignored |
| **Batch dependencies** | Supported (SLURM) | Supported (sequential) | Ignored |
| **stdout/stderr** | Written to log files | Written to log files | Streamed to notebook |
| **GPU allocation** | Requested via Resources() | Uses available GPUs | Colab-assigned |
| **Use case** | Production, large-scale | Local testing, small jobs | Prototyping, learning |

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:127-136](), [Docs/UserManual.md:162-171](), [Docs/UserManual.md:421-454]()

---

# Page: Tool Categories

# Tool Categories

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [Docs/Tool/Analysis.md](Docs/Tool/Analysis.md)
- [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md](Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md)
- [Docs/ToolReference.md](Docs/ToolReference.md)
- [Docs/UserManual.md](Docs/UserManual.md)
- [config.yaml](config.yaml)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

BioPipelines organizes its tools into six major functional categories that represent the typical workflow stages of computational protein design and analysis. This page provides an overview of these categories, their relationships, and the tools available in each.

For detailed documentation of individual tools, see the category-specific pages: [Utilities](#5.1), [Structure Generation](#5.2), [Sequence Design](#5.3), [Structure Prediction](#5.4), [Analysis](#5.5), [Data Management](#5.6), and [Visualization](#5.7).

For information about how tools inherit from `BaseConfig` and integrate with the framework, see [Tools and BaseConfig](#3.2).

Sources: [Docs/ToolReference.md:1-98]()

---

## Category Overview

BioPipelines tools are organized into functional categories that mirror typical computational protein design workflows:

| Category | Purpose | Importance Score | Typical Position in Workflow |
|----------|---------|------------------|------------------------------|
| **Utilities** | Data input, retrieval, and MSA generation | 48.13 | Start (input) or middle (MSA) |
| **Structure Generation** | De novo backbone design and generation | 47.09 | Early stage (after input) |
| **Sequence Design** | Sequence optimization for fixed backbones | 46.51 | Middle stage (after structure generation) |
| **Structure Prediction** | Structure prediction and docking | 50.21 | Middle-to-late (validation) |
| **Analysis** | Geometric and interaction analysis | 52.66 | Late stage (evaluation) |
| **Data Management** | Filtering, ranking, and ID manipulation | 52.66 | Any stage (iterative refinement) |
| **Visualization** | Rendering and plotting | N/A | End stage (presentation) |

**Importance scores** reflect the combined complexity and usage frequency of tools in each category, calculated from cluster analysis of the codebase ([see high-level diagrams]()).

Sources: [Docs/ToolReference.md:1-98](), [Docs/UserManual.md:1-611]()

---

## Tool Workflow Architecture

The following diagram illustrates how tool categories form a directed acyclic graph (DAG) representing typical computational protein design workflows:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Utilities["Utilities (Importance: 48.13)"]
        PDB["PDB<br/>Local/RCSB fetch"]
        RCSB["RCSB<br/>Search API"]
        Sequence["Sequence<br/>From strings/files"]
        Ligand["Ligand<br/>CCD/PubChem/SMILES"]
        CompoundLibrary["CompoundLibrary<br/>Chemical collections"]
        Load["Load/LoadMultiple<br/>Previous outputs"]
        MMseqs2["MMseqs2<br/>MSA generation"]
    end
    
    subgraph StructureGen["Structure Generation (Importance: 47.09)"]
        RFdiffusion["RFdiffusion<br/>Backbone generation"]
        RFdiffusion3["RFdiffusion3<br/>3rd gen design"]
        RFdiffusionAA["RFdiffusionAllAtom<br/>All-atom with ligands"]
        BoltzGen["BoltzGen<br/>End-to-end binder design"]
    end
    
    subgraph SeqDesign["Sequence Design (Importance: 46.51)"]
        ProteinMPNN["ProteinMPNN<br/>Fixed backbone design"]
        LigandMPNN["LigandMPNN<br/>Ligand-aware design"]
        MutationComposer["MutationComposer<br/>Combinatorial mutants"]
        Fuse["Fuse<br/>Fusion proteins + linkers"]
        StitchSequences["StitchSequences<br/>Substitutions + indels"]
    end
    
    subgraph StructurePred["Structure Prediction (Importance: 50.21)"]
        AlphaFold["AlphaFold<br/>AF2 predictions"]
        Boltz2["Boltz2<br/>Biomolecular complexes<br/>Affinity calculation"]
        Gnina["Gnina<br/>CNN-based docking"]
    end
    
    subgraph Analysis["Analysis Tools (Importance: 52.66)"]
        Distance["Distance<br/>Atom/residue distances"]
        Angle["Angle<br/>Bond/torsional/vector angles"]
        DistanceSelector["DistanceSelector<br/>Proximity-based selection"]
        Contacts["Contacts<br/>Protein-ligand interactions"]
        ConformationalChange["ConformationalChange<br/>RMSD analysis"]
        PoseBusters["PoseBusters<br/>Pose validation"]
        CABSflex["CABSflex<br/>Flexibility simulation"]
    end
    
    subgraph DataMgmt["Data Management (Importance: 52.66)"]
        Panda["Panda<br/>filter, sort, merge<br/>calculate, rank, groupby"]
        ReMap["ReMap<br/>ID management"]
        Selection["Selection<br/>PyMOL selection ops"]
        ExtractMetrics["ExtractMetrics<br/>Export for Prism"]
    end
    
    subgraph Visualization["Visualization"]
        PyMOL["PyMOL<br/>Sessions + images"]
        Plot["Plot<br/>Scatter, histogram, heatmap"]
    end
    
    PDB --> RFdiffusion
    RCSB --> RFdiffusion
    Ligand --> RFdiffusionAA
    Ligand --> BoltzGen
    Ligand --> Boltz2
    
    RFdiffusion --> ProteinMPNN
    RFdiffusion3 --> ProteinMPNN
    BoltzGen --> LigandMPNN
    
    ProteinMPNN --> AlphaFold
    LigandMPNN --> Boltz2
    StitchSequences --> AlphaFold
    
    AlphaFold --> Distance
    Boltz2 --> Contacts
    Boltz2 --> PoseBusters
    Gnina --> PoseBusters
    
    Distance --> Panda
    Contacts --> Panda
    PoseBusters --> Panda
    
    Panda --> ReMap
    Panda --> PyMOL
    Panda --> Plot
    
    DistanceSelector --> LigandMPNN
    Selection --> ProteinMPNN
    
    MMseqs2 --> Boltz2
    MMseqs2 --> AlphaFold
```

**Critical feedback loops**:
- `DistanceSelector` → `LigandMPNN`: Enables binding site-focused sequence design
- `Selection` → `ProteinMPNN`: Enables position-selective redesign
- `Panda` → upstream tools: Enables filtering-driven iterative refinement
- `MMseqs2` → structure prediction: Accelerates predictions by providing MSAs

Sources: [Docs/UserManual.md:1-611](), [Docs/ToolReference.md:1-98]()

---

## Utilities

**Purpose**: Provide data input, retrieval, and preprocessing capabilities. These tools are typically used at the start of workflows to fetch structures, define sequences, or generate MSAs.

**Tools**:

| Tool | Class Name | Purpose | Helper Script(s) |
|------|------------|---------|------------------|
| **PDB** | `PDB` | Fetch protein structures from local folders or RCSB | [HelpScripts/pipe_pdb.py]() |
| **RCSB** | `RCSB` | Search RCSB PDB and download multiple structures | [HelpScripts/pipe_pdb.py]() |
| **Sequence** | `Sequence` | Create sequences from strings, lists, or files | [HelpScripts/pipe_sequence.py]() |
| **Ligand** | `Ligand` | Fetch small molecules from RCSB CCD, PubChem, or SMILES | [HelpScripts/pipe_ligand.py]() |
| **CompoundLibrary** | `CompoundLibrary` | Create compound collections with R-group expansion | [biopipelines/compound_library.py]() |
| **Load** | `Load` | Load previous tool outputs | [biopipelines/load.py]() |
| **LoadMultiple** | `LoadMultiple` | Load multiple outputs by tool name | [biopipelines/load.py]() |
| **MMseqs2** | `MMseqs2` | MSA generation via distributed server | [HelpScripts/pipe_mmseqs2_sequences.py]() |

**Key Features**:
- Priority-based lookup: local → repository cache → external database ([config.yaml:25-60]())
- Format conversion and standardization (PDB ↔ CIF, SMILES → 3D)
- MSA generation via client-server architecture with automatic retry

**Detailed Documentation**: See [Utilities](#5.1)

Sources: [Docs/ToolReference.md:7-25](), [Docs/UserManual.md:222-326](), [config.yaml:25-60]()

---

## Structure Generation

**Purpose**: Generate novel protein backbones and structures using diffusion-based generative models. These tools create the structural scaffolds upon which sequences will be designed.

**Tools**:

| Tool | Class Name | Purpose | Helper Script(s) |
|------|------------|---------|------------------|
| **RFdiffusion** | `RFdiffusion` | Backbone generation with contig specification | [HelpScripts/pipe_rfdiffusion.py]() |
| **RFdiffusion3** | `RFdiffusion3` | Third-generation design with advanced features | [HelpScripts/pipe_rfdiffusion3_postprocess.py](), [HelpScripts/pipe_rfdiffusion3_table.py]() |
| **RFdiffusionAllAtom** | `RFdiffusionAllAtom` | All-atom design with ligand support | [HelpScripts/pipe_rfdaa_prepare_ligand.py]() |
| **BoltzGen** | `BoltzGen` | End-to-end binder design with inverse folding | [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen.py](), [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen_import.py](), [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen_merge.py]() |

**Key Features**:
- Contig-based specification of fixed and designed regions
- Constraint support (hotspots, symmetry, secondary structure)
- All-atom modeling with small molecule ligands
- Integration with sequence design (BoltzGen combines generation + sequence design)

**Environments**: `SE3nv` (RFdiffusion, RFdiffusionAllAtom), `foundry` (RFdiffusion3), `boltzgen` (BoltzGen)

**Detailed Documentation**: See [Structure Generation Tools](#5.2)

Sources: [Docs/ToolReference.md:28-36](), [config.yaml:66-72]()

---

## Sequence Design

**Purpose**: Design and optimize amino acid sequences for fixed protein backbones. These tools enable position-specific design, combinatorial mutagenesis, and protein fusion.

**Tools**:

| Tool | Class Name | Purpose | Helper Script(s) |
|------|------------|---------|------------------|
| **ProteinMPNN** | `ProteinMPNN` | Sequence design for backbones | [HelpScripts/pipe_pmpnn_fixed_positions.py]() |
| **LigandMPNN** | `LigandMPNN` | Ligand-aware sequence design | [HelpScripts/pipe_lmpnn_runtime_positions.py]() |
| **MutationComposer** | `MutationComposer` | Combinatorial mutant library generation | Tool-specific |
| **Mutagenesis** | `Mutagenesis` | Systematic single/double mutations | Tool-specific |
| **Fuse** | `Fuse` | Fusion proteins with flexible linkers | Tool-specific |
| **StitchSequences** | `StitchSequences` | Sequence substitutions and indels | [HelpScripts/pipe_stitch_sequences.py]() |
| **DNAEncoder** | `DNAEncoder` | Codon optimization | Tool-specific |
| **RBSDesigner** | `RBSDesigner` | Ribosome binding site design | Tool-specific |

**Key Features**:
- Position-selective design via fixed/redesigned specifications
- Column reference support for dynamic position selection ([see Table Column References](#3.4))
- Combinatorial expansion of mutation combinations
- Linker design for fusion proteins

**Environments**: `SE3nv` (ProteinMPNN), `ligandmpnn_env` (LigandMPNN), `MutationEnv` (MutationComposer, Mutagenesis), `biopipelines` (others)

**Detailed Documentation**: See [Sequence Design Tools](#5.3)

Sources: [Docs/ToolReference.md:39-51](), [config.yaml:74-82](), [HelpScripts/pipe_stitch_sequences.py]()

---

## Structure Prediction

**Purpose**: Predict 3D structures from sequences, model biomolecular complexes, and dock ligands. These tools validate designed sequences and predict binding modes.

**Tools**:

| Tool | Class Name | Purpose | Helper Script(s) |
|------|------------|---------|------------------|
| **AlphaFold** | `AlphaFold` | AlphaFold2 structure prediction | Wrapper around LocalColabFold |
| **Boltz2** | `Boltz2` | Biomolecular complex prediction with constraints | [HelpScripts/pipe_boltz_config_unified.py](), [HelpScripts/pipe_boltz_postprocessing.py]() |
| **Gnina** | `Gnina` | CNN-based molecular docking | Tool-specific |

**Key Features**:
- **AlphaFold**: Fast predictions using LocalColabFold, MSA support
- **Boltz2**: Multi-entity complexes (protein, RNA, DNA, ligands), constraint system (template, pocket, glycosylation, covalent linkage, contacts), affinity calculation, MSA recycling
- **Gnina**: CNN scoring function, exhaustive and local docking modes

**Boltz2 Constraint Types**:
- `template`: Fix backbone coordinates
- `pocket`: Define binding pocket residues
- `glycosylation`: N-glycosylation sites
- `covalent_linkage`: Covalent bonds between entities
- `contacts`: Predicted inter-entity contacts

**Environments**: `biopipelines` (AlphaFold, Gnina), `Boltz2Env` (Boltz2)

**Detailed Documentation**: See [Structure Prediction Tools](#5.4) and [Boltz2 Workflow](#6.1)

Sources: [Docs/ToolReference.md:54-61](), [config.yaml:84-88](), [Docs/UserManual.md:1-611]()

---

## Analysis

**Purpose**: Analyze structural properties, interactions, and pose quality. These tools provide quantitative metrics for filtering and ranking designed structures.

**Tools**:

| Tool | Class Name | Purpose | Output Metrics |
|------|------------|---------|----------------|
| **Distance** | `Distance` | Atom/residue distance measurements | Custom metric name (default: "distance") |
| **Angle** | `Angle` | Bond, torsional, and vector-vector angles | Custom metric name (default: "angle"/"torsion"/"vector_angle") |
| **DistanceSelector** | `DistanceSelector` | Proximity-based residue selection | `within`, `beyond` (PyMOL selection strings) |
| **Contacts** | `Contacts` | Protein-ligand contact analysis | `contacts`, `min_distance`, `max_distance`, `mean_distance` |
| **ConformationalChange** | `ConformationalChange` | Structure alignment and RMSD | `RMSD`, `num_aligned_atoms` |
| **PoseBusters** | `PoseBusters` | Pose validation suite | 13 validation checks + `all_pass` |
| **PoseChange** | `PoseChange` | Ligand pose comparison | `ligand_rmsd`, `centroid_distance`, `alignment_rmsd` |
| **CABSflex** | `CABSflex` | Protein flexibility simulation | Per-residue RMSF, ensemble structures |

**Analysis Workflow Pattern**:

```mermaid
graph LR
    StructurePred["Structure Prediction<br/>(AlphaFold, Boltz2, Gnina)"]
    GeometricAnalysis["Geometric Analysis<br/>(Distance, Angle, Contacts)"]
    ValidationAnalysis["Validation Analysis<br/>(PoseBusters, ConformationalChange)"]
    Panda["Panda<br/>(Filter, Rank, Merge)"]
    FilteredStructures["Filtered Structures<br/>(via pool mode)"]
    
    StructurePred --> GeometricAnalysis
    StructurePred --> ValidationAnalysis
    GeometricAnalysis --> Panda
    ValidationAnalysis --> Panda
    Panda --> FilteredStructures
```

**Key Features**:
- Custom metric naming for downstream filtering
- PyMOL-based selection syntax
- Support for table column references (e.g., `designed` residues from RFdiffusion)
- Integration with `Panda` for metric-based filtering

**Environments**: `biopipelines` (Distance, Angle, DistanceSelector, Gnina), `ProteinEnv` (Contacts, ConformationalChange, PoseChange), `posebusters` (PoseBusters), `CABSflex` (CABSflex)

**Detailed Documentation**: See [Analysis Tools](#5.5)

Sources: [Docs/Tool/Analysis.md:1-458](), [config.yaml:93-105]()

---

## Data Management

**Purpose**: Transform, filter, and manipulate tables and data streams. These tools enable iterative refinement and ID management across workflows.

**Tools**:

| Tool | Class Name | Purpose | Key Operations |
|------|------------|---------|----------------|
| **Panda** | `Panda` | Unified pandas-style transformations | `filter`, `sort`, `merge`, `concat`, `calculate`, `rank`, `groupby` |
| **ReMap** | `ReMap` | Rename IDs across streams and tables | Auto-numbering, explicit mapping, alignment onto other tools |
| **Selection** | `Selection` | PyMOL selection string manipulation | `add`, `subtract`, `expand`, `shrink`, `shift`, `invert` |
| **ExtractMetrics** | `ExtractMetrics` | Export metrics for GraphPad Prism | Per-metric CSV files with columns per condition |

**Panda Operations** (comprehensive list):

```mermaid
graph TB
    Input["Input Tables"]
    
    subgraph "Row Operations"
        Filter["filter(expr)"]
        Sort["sort(by, ascending)"]
        Head["head(n)"]
        Tail["tail(n)"]
        Sample["sample(n, frac)"]
        DropDuplicates["drop_duplicates(subset)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Column Operations"
        Calculate["calculate(exprs)"]
        SelectColumns["select_columns(cols)"]
        DropColumns["drop_columns(cols)"]
        Rename["rename(mapping)"]
        FillNA["fillna(value)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Multi-Table Operations"
        Merge["merge(on, how, prefixes)"]
        Concat["concat(fill, add_source)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Aggregation Operations"
        Rank["rank(by, prefix)"]
        GroupBy["groupby(by, agg)"]
        Pivot["pivot(index, columns, values)"]
        Melt["melt(id_vars)"]
        AvgBySource["average_by_source()"]
    end
    
    Output["Output Table<br/>+ Optional Streams (pool mode)"]
    
    Input --> Filter
    Input --> Calculate
    Input --> Merge
    Input --> Rank
    
    Filter --> Output
    Calculate --> Output
    Merge --> Output
    Rank --> Output
```

**Pool Mode**: When `pool` parameter is provided, `Panda` copies files (structures, sequences, compounds) matching filtered IDs, enabling metric-based structure selection.

**Rename Mode**: When `rename` parameter is provided, output IDs are renumbered (e.g., `best_1`, `best_2`, ...).

**Environments**: All data management tools use `biopipelines` environment (except `Selection` which uses `ProteinEnv`)

**Detailed Documentation**: See [Data Management Tools](#5.6)

Sources: [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:1-247](), [Docs/UserManual.md:497-551]()

---

## Visualization

**Purpose**: Generate visual representations of structures and data for analysis and presentation.

**Tools**:

| Tool | Class Name | Purpose | Output Formats |
|------|------------|---------|----------------|
| **PyMOL** | `PyMOL` | PyMOL session and image generation | PSE sessions, PNG images |
| **Plot** | `Plot` | Statistical plots | PNG images, CSV data |

**PyMOL Features**:
- Declarative operation system (color, hide, show, zoom, etc.)
- Automatic session creation
- Batch image rendering

**Plot Types**:
- Scatter plots
- Histograms
- Bar charts
- Column charts
- Heatmaps

**Environments**: `ProteinEnv` (PyMOL), `biopipelines` (Plot)

**Detailed Documentation**: See [Visualization Tools](#5.7)

Sources: [Docs/ToolReference.md:22-25](), [config.yaml:119-120]()

## Category Relationships and Data Flow

The following diagram shows how data flows between categories using the `StandardizedOutput` and `DataStream` types:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Stage"
        Utilities_Input["Utilities<br/>(PDB, Sequence, Ligand, CompoundLibrary)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Generation Stage"
        StructureGen["Structure Generation<br/>(RFdiffusion, BoltzGen)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Design Stage"
        SeqDesign["Sequence Design<br/>(ProteinMPNN, LigandMPNN)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Prediction Stage"
        StructurePred["Structure Prediction<br/>(AlphaFold, Boltz2)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Analysis Stage"
        Analysis["Analysis<br/>(Distance, Contacts, PoseBusters)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Refinement Stage"
        DataMgmt["Data Management<br/>(Panda, ReMap, Selection)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Stage"
        Visualization["Visualization<br/>(PyMOL, Plot)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Support Services"
        MMseqs2_Support["MMseqs2<br/>(MSA generation)"]
        Load_Support["Load/LoadMultiple<br/>(Resume workflows)"]
    end
    
    Utilities_Input -->|"streams.structures<br/>streams.sequences<br/>streams.compounds"| StructureGen
    Utilities_Input -->|"streams.structures"| SeqDesign
    
    StructureGen -->|"streams.structures<br/>tables.structures"| SeqDesign
    
    SeqDesign -->|"streams.sequences"| StructurePred
    Utilities_Input -->|"streams.compounds"| StructurePred
    
    StructurePred -->|"streams.structures<br/>tables.confidence"| Analysis
    
    Analysis -->|"tables.distances<br/>tables.contacts<br/>tables.posebusters"| DataMgmt
    StructurePred -->|"tables.affinity"| DataMgmt
    
    DataMgmt -->|"tables.result<br/>streams.structures (pool)"| Visualization
    DataMgmt -.->|"Feedback loop<br/>column references"| SeqDesign
    
    MMseqs2_Support -->|"streams.msas"| StructurePred
    Load_Support -->|"Any streams/tables"| DataMgmt
```

**Key Data Types**:
- **`DataStream`**: ID-tracked file collections (PDB, FASTA, SDF, A3M) or value tables (sequences, compounds)
- **`StandardizedOutput`**: Container with `StreamContainer` (`.streams.structures`, `.streams.sequences`, etc.) and `TableContainer` (`.tables.confidence`, `.tables.affinity`, etc.)
- **Column References**: Tuple `(TableInfo, "column_name")` enabling metadata-driven parameterization

**Feedback Mechanism**: Tools like `DistanceSelector` and `Selection` analyze structures and produce position specifications (stored in tables), which are then passed to sequence design tools via column references. This enables structure-informed sequence design.

Sources: [Docs/UserManual.md:172-220](), [Docs/UserManual.md:373-392]()

# Utilities

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [Docs/Tool/Analysis.md](Docs/Tool/Analysis.md)
- [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md](Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md)
- [Docs/ToolReference.md](Docs/ToolReference.md)
- [HelpScripts/pipe_ligand.py](HelpScripts/pipe_ligand.py)
- [HelpScripts/pipe_pdb.py](HelpScripts/pipe_pdb.py)
- [HelpScripts/pipe_rfdaa_prepare_ligand.py](HelpScripts/pipe_rfdaa_prepare_ligand.py)
- [HelpScripts/pipe_rfdiffusion3_postprocess.py](HelpScripts/pipe_rfdiffusion3_postprocess.py)

</details>



Utility tools provide data input and loading functionality for BioPipelines workflows. They fetch, create, or load input entities (structures, sequences, ligands, compounds) that serve as starting points for design and prediction tools. All utility tools output `StandardizedOutput` objects with typed streams (`DataStream`) and tables (`TableInfo`), enabling seamless integration with downstream tools.

For visualization tools (PyMOL, Plot), see [Visualization Tools](#5.7). For data transformation tools (Panda, ReMap, Selection), see [Data Management Tools](#5.6).

---

## Architecture Overview

All utility tools follow a common two-phase execution model: configuration (Python) predicts outputs and generates scripts, execution (Bash) performs actual work via helper scripts.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Utility Tool Categories"
        StructInput["Structure Input<br/>PDB, RCSB"]
        SeqInput["Sequence Input<br/>Sequence"]
        LigandInput["Ligand Input<br/>Ligand, CompoundLibrary"]
        MSAInput["MSA Input<br/>MMseqs2"]
        LoadInput["Pipeline Input<br/>Load, LoadMultiple"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Common Output Types"
        Structures["DataStream: structures<br/>.pdb or .cif files"]
        Sequences["DataStream: sequences<br/>.fasta or .csv"]
        Compounds["DataStream: compounds<br/>.pdb/.cif or .sdf"]
        MSAs["DataStream: msas<br/>.a3m files"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Downstream Tools"
        StructGen["Structure Generation<br/>RFdiffusion, BoltzGen"]
        SeqDesign["Sequence Design<br/>ProteinMPNN, LigandMPNN"]
        Prediction["Structure Prediction<br/>AlphaFold, Boltz2"]
    end
    
    StructInput --> Structures
    SeqInput --> Sequences
    LigandInput --> Compounds
    MSAInput --> MSAs
    LoadInput --> Structures
    LoadInput --> Sequences
    LoadInput --> Compounds
    
    Structures --> StructGen
    Structures --> Prediction
    Sequences --> SeqDesign
    Sequences --> Prediction
    Compounds --> StructGen
    Compounds --> Prediction
    MSAs --> Prediction
```

**Sources:** Docs/ToolReference.md:1-98, High-level diagrams (Diagram 1, Diagram 3)

---

## PDB: Structure Fetching

The `PDB` tool fetches protein structures using a priority-based lookup: local folder → repository `PDBs/` folder → RCSB download. Downloads are cached in `PDBs/` for reuse across pipelines.

### Priority-Based Lookup

```mermaid
graph LR
    Request["PDB(pdbs='4UFC')"]
    
    CheckLocal["Check local_folder<br/>(if provided)"]
    CheckRepo["Check PDBs/<br/>(repository cache)"]
    DownloadRCSB["Download from RCSB<br/>data.rcsb.org"]
    
    CacheRepo["Cache to PDBs/"]
    CopyOutput["Copy to ToolOutputs/"]
    
    Success["Return structure path<br/>+ metadata"]
    
    Request --> CheckLocal
    CheckLocal -->|"Not found"| CheckRepo
    CheckLocal -->|"Found"| CopyOutput
    CheckRepo -->|"Not found"| DownloadRCSB
    CheckRepo -->|"Found"| CopyOutput
    DownloadRCSB --> CacheRepo
    CacheRepo --> CopyOutput
    CopyOutput --> Success
```

**Sources:** HelpScripts/pipe_pdb.py:569-628, biopipelines/pdb.py:304-396

### Format Conversion

The `PDB` tool supports flexible format handling via the `convert` parameter:

| `convert` value | Behavior |
|-----------------|----------|
| `None` (default) | Keep whatever format found locally or downloaded (no conversion) |
| `"pdb"` | Convert to PDB format (CIF → PDB if needed) |
| `"cif"` | Convert to CIF format (PDB → CIF not yet implemented) |

CIF to PDB conversion uses BioPython's `MMCIFParser` and `PDBIO`.

**Sources:** HelpScripts/pipe_pdb.py:28-78, biopipelines/pdb.py:109-223

### Operations

PDB supports post-load operations via positional arguments. Currently supports `PDB.Rename(old, new)` for residue renaming.

```python
from biopipelines.pdb import PDB

# Rename ligand residue (useful for RFdiffusion3 compatibility)
pdb = PDB(
    pdbs="rifampicin.pdb",
    PDB.Rename("LIG", ":L:")
)

# Multiple renames
pdb = PDB(
    pdbs="4ufc",
    PDB.Rename("ATP", ":A:"),
    PDB.Rename("GDP", ":G:")
)
```

Operations are applied in sequence after fetching/conversion. The rename operation modifies PDB residue name field (columns 17-19, 0-indexed 17:20).

**Sources:** biopipelines/pdb.py:27-106, HelpScripts/pipe_pdb.py:119-174

### Sequence Extraction

PDB automatically extracts protein sequences from structures. By default, returns the longest chain to avoid inflating memory in downstream tools (multi-chain complexes often contain identical chains).

```python
# Default: longest chain
pdb = PDB(pdbs="4ufc")  # Extracts sequence from longest chain

# Specific chain
pdb = PDB(pdbs="4ufc", chain="A")  # Extract chain A only

# Keep entire structure but extract specific chain sequence
pdb = PDB(pdbs="4ufc", chain="E")  # Sequence from chain E
```

**Sources:** HelpScripts/pipe_pdb.py:279-337, HelpScripts/pipe_pdb.py:339-433

### Ligand Detection

PDB automatically detects ligands (HETATM records excluding waters, ions, crystallization agents) and fetches SMILES strings from RCSB REST API.

**Exclusion list:** HOH, WAT, H2O, SOL, NA, CL, K, CA, MG, ZN, SO4, PO4, GOL, EDO, PEG, ACT, BME, etc.

**Sources:** HelpScripts/pipe_pdb.py:436-567, HelpScripts/pipe_pdb.py:515-566

### Output Specification

```mermaid
graph TB
    PDBTool["PDB tool instance"]
    
    subgraph "Streams"
        S_structures["structures<br/>format: 'pdb' | 'cif' | 'pdb|cif'<br/>map_table: structures.csv"]
        S_sequences["sequences<br/>format: 'csv'<br/>map_table: sequences.csv"]
        S_compounds["compounds<br/>format: 'pdb' | 'cif'<br/>map_table: compounds.csv"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Tables"
        T_structures["structures.csv<br/>id | pdb_id | file_path | format | file_size | source"]
        T_sequences["sequences.csv<br/>id | sequence | length"]
        T_compounds["compounds.csv<br/>id | code | format | smiles | ccd"]
        T_failed["failed_downloads.csv<br/>pdb_id | error_message | source | attempted_path"]
    end
    
    PDBTool --> S_structures
    PDBTool --> S_sequences
    PDBTool --> S_compounds
    
    S_structures -.references.-> T_structures
    S_sequences -.references.-> T_sequences
    S_compounds -.references.-> T_compounds
    PDBTool --> T_failed
```

**Sources:** biopipelines/pdb.py:77-83, HelpScripts/pipe_pdb.py:1445-1513

### Helper Script: pipe_pdb.py

The runtime execution is handled by `pipe_pdb.py`, which implements:

- **Priority lookup logic:** [HelpScripts/pipe_pdb.py:569-628]()
- **RCSB download:** [HelpScripts/pipe_pdb.py:738-930]()
- **CIF→PDB conversion:** [HelpScripts/pipe_pdb.py:28-78]()
- **Water removal:** [HelpScripts/pipe_pdb.py:177-203]()
- **Chain filtering:** [HelpScripts/pipe_pdb.py:206-276]()
- **Sequence extraction:** [HelpScripts/pipe_pdb.py:279-337]()
- **Ligand detection:** [HelpScripts/pipe_pdb.py:436-512]()
- **SMILES fetching:** [HelpScripts/pipe_pdb.py:515-566]()
- **Operations (rename):** [HelpScripts/pipe_pdb.py:97-174]()

**Sources:** HelpScripts/pipe_pdb.py:1-1513

## RCSB: Search API Integration

The `RCSB` tool provides programmatic access to the RCSB PDB Search API v2, enabling structure discovery based on text, attributes, sequence similarity, structure similarity, and chemical similarity.

### Query Construction

RCSB uses a typed attribute system via `StructureAttribute` namespace, which mirrors the RCSB advanced search interface:

```python
from biopipelines.rcsb import RCSB, StructureAttribute, PolymerEntityType, SymmetryType

# Attribute-based search
results = RCSB(
    StructureAttribute.NonpolymerFeatures.ComponentIdentifier.is_any("FMN", "FAD"),
    StructureAttribute.PolymerMolecularFeatures.PolymerEntityType.equals(PolymerEntityType.PROTEIN),
    StructureAttribute.AssemblyFeatures.SymmetryType.equals(SymmetryType.ASYMMETRIC),
    StructureAttribute.PolymerMolecularFeatures.PolymerEntitySequenceLength.between(80, 300),
    max_results=100
)
```

### Attribute Categories

```mermaid
graph TB
    StructAttr["StructureAttribute namespace"]
    
    IDsKw["IDsAndKeywords<br/>EntryId, StructureKeywords"]
    Details["StructureDetails<br/>StructureTitle, DepositDate, ReleaseDate"]
    EntryFeat["EntryFeatures<br/>MolecularWeight, NumberOfProteinEntities"]
    PolymerFeat["PolymerMolecularFeatures<br/>PolymerEntityType, SequenceLength, GeneName"]
    NonPolymer["NonpolymerFeatures<br/>ComponentIdentifier, FormulaWeight"]
    Assembly["AssemblyFeatures<br/>SymmetryType, OligomericState"]
    Methods["Methods<br/>ExperimentalMethod, Resolution"]
    
    StructAttr --> IDsKw
    StructAttr --> Details
    StructAttr --> EntryFeat
    StructAttr --> PolymerFeat
    StructAttr --> NonPolymer
    StructAttr --> Assembly
    StructAttr --> Methods
```

**Sources:** biopipelines/rcsb.py:169-252

### Comparison Methods

Each attribute descriptor exposes typed comparison methods:

| Method | Description | Example |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `equals(value)` | Exact match | `.equals(PolymerEntityType.PROTEIN)` |
| `is_any(*values)` | One of multiple values | `.is_any("FMN", "FAD")` |
| `contains(text)` | Case-insensitive substring | `.contains("kinase")` |
| `contains_phrase(text)` | Exact phrase | `.contains_phrase("insulin receptor")` |
| `between(low, high)` | Numeric/date range | `.between(80, 300)` |
| `greater_than(value)` | Numeric comparison | `.greater_than(2.5)` |
| `less_than(value)` | Numeric comparison | `.less_than(2.0)` |
| `exists()` | Attribute has value | `.exists()` |
| `not_equals(value)` | Negation | `.not_equals(PolymerEntityType.DNA)` |
| `not_any(*values)` | Exclude values | `.not_any("HOH", "WAT")` |

**Sources:** biopipelines/rcsb.py:80-167

### Static Query Constructors

For non-attribute searches, use static methods:

```python
# Text search (full-text)
RCSB(RCSB.Text("insulin receptor + human"), max_results=10)

# Sequence similarity (BLAST-like)
RCSB(RCSB.Sequence("MKTVRQERLK...", identity_cutoff=0.9), max_results=50)

# Structure similarity
RCSB(RCSB.Structure("4HHB", assembly_id=1), max_results=10)

# Sequence motif (PROSITE format)
RCSB(RCSB.SeqMotif("C-x(2,4)-C-x(3)-[LIVMFYWC]-x(8)-H", pattern_type="prosite"))

# Chemical similarity (SMILES-based)
RCSB(RCSB.Chemical("c1ccc(cc1)C(=O)O", match_type="fingerprint-similarity"))
```

**Sources:** biopipelines/rcsb.py:350-467

### Execution Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant RCSBTool["RCSB tool"]
    participant SearchAPI["RCSB Search API v2"]
    participant PipePDB["pipe_pdb.py"]
    participant RCSBFiles["files.rcsb.org"]
    
    User->>RCSBTool: RCSB(query, max_results=100)
    
    rect rgb(230, 245, 255)
        Note over RCSBTool: Configuration Phase
        RCSBTool->>SearchAPI: POST query JSON
        SearchAPI-->>RCSBTool: Return PDB IDs
        RCSBTool->>RCSBTool: Predict output files
        RCSBTool->>RCSBTool: Generate fetch_config.json
    end
    
    rect rgb(255, 245, 230)
        Note over PipePDB: Execution Phase
        RCSBTool->>PipePDB: python pipe_pdb.py --config fetch_config.json
        loop For each PDB ID
            PipePDB->>PipePDB: Check local / PDBs/
            PipePDB->>RCSBFiles: Download if needed
            PipePDB->>PipePDB: Extract sequence, ligands
        end
        PipePDB->>PipePDB: Write structures.csv, sequences.csv
    end
```

**Sources:** biopipelines/rcsb.py:254-721

### Output

RCSB produces identical output to PDB tool:
- **Streams:** `structures`, `sequences`, `compounds`
- **Tables:** `structures.csv`, `sequences.csv`, `compounds.csv`, `failed_downloads.csv`, `search_results.csv`

The `search_results.csv` contains the raw search API response with scores and metadata.

**Sources:** biopipelines/rcsb.py:341-348, biopipelines/rcsb.py:671-721

---

## Ligand: Small Molecule Fetching

The `Ligand` tool fetches small molecules from multiple sources with automatic format detection and 3D coordinate generation.

### Lookup Type Detection

```mermaid
graph TB
    Input["Ligand lookup value"]
    
    DetectType["detect_lookup_type()"]
    
    CCD["CCD code<br/>1-3 uppercase alphanumeric<br/>not purely numeric<br/>Example: ATP, FMN"]
    CID["PubChem CID<br/>purely numeric<br/>Example: 5957"]
    CAS["CAS number<br/>XX-XX-X format<br/>Example: 50-81-7"]
    Name["Compound name<br/>default fallback<br/>Example: 'aspirin'"]
    SMILES["SMILES string<br/>Ligand(smiles='...')"]
    
    Input --> DetectType
    DetectType --> CCD
    DetectType --> CID
    DetectType --> CAS
    DetectType --> Name
    Input --> SMILES
```

**Sources:** HelpScripts/pipe_ligand.py:25-49

### Priority-Based Lookup (Non-SMILES)

Similar to PDB, Ligand uses priority-based file lookup:

1. **local_folder** (if provided)
2. **Ligands/** (repository cache)
3. **RCSB CCD** (for CCD codes) or **PubChem** (for CID/CAS/name)

**Sources:** HelpScripts/pipe_ligand.py:51-83

### SMILES to 3D Conversion

For direct SMILES input or when downloading from PubChem/RCSB returns only SMILES, the tool generates 3D coordinates:

```mermaid
graph TB
    SMILES["SMILES string"]
    
    RDKit["RDKit available?"]
    OpenBabel["OpenBabel available?"]
    
    RDKitConv["convert_smiles_to_pdb_rdkit()<br/>or convert_smiles_to_cif_rdkit()"]
    OBConv["convert_smiles_to_sdf_openbabel()<br/>then sdf_to_pdb()"]
    
    PDB["Output: .pdb or .cif<br/>with 3D coordinates"]
    
    SMILES --> RDKit
    RDKit -->|"Yes"| RDKitConv
    RDKit -->|"No"| OpenBabel
    OpenBabel -->|"Yes"| OBConv
    OpenBabel -->|"No"| Error["Error: No converter available"]
    
    RDKitConv --> PDB
    OBConv --> PDB
```

**RDKit method (preferred):**
- Parse SMILES with `Chem.MolFromSmiles()`
- Add hydrogens: `Chem.AddHs()`
- Generate 3D: `AllChem.EmbedMolecule()` with ETKDG v3
- Optimize: `AllChem.MMFFOptimizeMolecule()`
- Remove hydrogens: `Chem.RemoveHs()`
- Export: `Chem.MolToPDBBlock()` or custom CIF generation

**Important:** RDKit atom naming is preserved for compatibility with tools like RFdiffusion3 that internally regenerate conformers.

**Sources:** HelpScripts/pipe_ligand.py:171-240, HelpScripts/pipe_ligand.py:243-385

### Format Conversion

The `convert` parameter controls output format:

| Value | Behavior |
|-------|----------|
| `None` (default) | Keep source format (PDB or CIF) |
| `"pdb"` | Convert to PDB |
| `"cif"` | Convert to CIF |

CIF output includes explicit bond information via `_chem_comp_bond` category (required by some tools like RFdiffusion3).

**Sources:** HelpScripts/pipe_ligand.py:243-385

### Residue Renaming

Ligand tool automatically renames residue codes to match the `residue_code` parameter:

```python
from biopipelines.ligand import Ligand

# Fetch ATP but rename to :A: for RFdiffusion3
lig = Ligand(ligands="ATP", residue_code=":A:")

# Custom SMILES with custom residue code
lig = Ligand(smiles="CCO", residue_code=":L:")
```

**Sources:** HelpScripts/pipe_ligand.py:388-491, HelpScripts/pipe_ligand.py:494-532

### Output Specification

```mermaid
graph TB
    LigandTool["Ligand tool instance"]
    
    subgraph "Streams"
        S_compounds["compounds<br/>format: 'pdb' | 'cif'<br/>map_table: compounds.csv"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Tables"
        T_compounds["compounds.csv<br/>id | code | format | smiles | ccd | name | formula"]
        T_failed["failed.csv<br/>lookup | error_message | source"]
    end
    
    LigandTool --> S_compounds
    S_compounds -.references.-> T_compounds
    LigandTool --> T_failed
```

**Sources:** HelpScripts/pipe_ligand.py:1240-1320

---

## Sequence: Sequence Creation

The `Sequence` tool creates sequence entities from raw amino acid or nucleotide strings.

### Usage

```python
from biopipelines.sequence import Sequence

# Single sequence
seq = Sequence(sequences="MKTVRQERLK", ids="kinase")

# Multiple sequences
seqs = Sequence(
    sequences=["MKTVRQERLK", "AAAAAAA"],
    ids=["seq1", "seq2"]
)

# Auto-numbering
seqs = Sequence(
    sequences=["MKTVRQERLK", "AAAAAAA"],
    ids="design"  # Outputs: design_1, design_2
)

# Specify type
dna = Sequence(sequences="ATCGATCG", type="dna")
```

### Execution Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant SeqTool["Sequence tool"]
    participant PipeSeq["pipe_sequence.py"]
    
    User->>SeqTool: Sequence(sequences=["MKTVR..."], ids=["seq1"])
    
    rect rgb(230, 245, 255)
        Note over SeqTool: Configuration Phase
        SeqTool->>SeqTool: Validate sequences (amino acid alphabet)
        SeqTool->>SeqTool: Predict IDs (auto-number if needed)
        SeqTool->>SeqTool: Generate config JSON
    end
    
    rect rgb(255, 245, 230)
        Note over PipeSeq: Execution Phase
        SeqTool->>PipeSeq: python pipe_sequence.py --config config.json
        PipeSeq->>PipeSeq: Read sequences from config
        PipeSeq->>PipeSeq: Clean whitespace
        PipeSeq->>PipeSeq: Write sequences.csv
        PipeSeq->>PipeSeq: Write sequences.fasta (80 char lines)
    end
```

**Sources:** HelpScripts/pipe_sequence.py:1-124

### Output

- **DataStream:** `sequences` (format: `"csv"`, map_table: `"sequences.csv"`)
- **TableInfo:** `sequences.csv` with columns: `id`, `sequence`, `type`, `length`
- **File:** `sequences.fasta` (FASTA format, not exposed as DataStream)

**Sources:** HelpScripts/pipe_sequence.py:20-80

---

## CompoundLibrary: Compound Collections

The `CompoundLibrary` tool creates collections of small molecules, either from explicit lists or from compound libraries (e.g., fragment libraries, drug-like compounds).

### Usage

```python
from biopipelines.compound_library import CompoundLibrary

# From explicit SMILES list
library = CompoundLibrary(
    smiles=["CCO", "c1ccccc1", "CC(=O)O"],
    ids=["ethanol", "benzene", "acetate"]
)

# From library name (predefined collections)
library = CompoundLibrary(library="fragments")

# With filters
library = CompoundLibrary(
    library="drugbank",
    mw_range=(200, 500),
    logp_range=(-1, 5)
)
```

### Output

Similar to Ligand tool:
- **DataStream:** `compounds` (3D structures as PDB/CIF)
- **TableInfo:** `compounds.csv` with SMILES, molecular properties

---

## Load / LoadMultiple: Pipeline Output Reuse

The `Load` and `LoadMultiple` tools enable reusing outputs from previous pipeline runs.

### Load: Single Tool Output

```python
from biopipelines.load import Load

# Load by job name
previous = Load(job="MyPreviousJob", tool="RFdiffusion", batch=1)

# Load by absolute path
previous = Load(folder="/path/to/ToolOutputs/Job_Tool_batch1")

# Access streams
previous.streams.structures
previous.tables.results
```

### LoadMultiple: Multiple Outputs

```python
from biopipelines.load import LoadMultiple

# Load multiple batches
all_batches = LoadMultiple(
    job="MyJob",
    tool="ProteinMPNN",
    batches=[1, 2, 3]
)

# Access merged streams
all_batches.streams.sequences  # All sequences combined
```

### Implementation

Load tools read the `ToolOutputs/` directory structure and reconstruct `StandardizedOutput` objects by parsing CSV files and discovering file streams.

---

## MMseqs2: Distributed MSA Generation

The `MMseqs2` tool generates Multiple Sequence Alignments via a client-server architecture that supports GPU acceleration and automatic server management.

### Client-Server Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Pipeline Execution"
        MMseqs2Tool["MMseqs2 tool instance"]
        PipeMMseqs2["pipe_mmseqs2_sequences.py<br/>(client script)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Shared Server Folder"
        Queue["Queue/<br/>*.fasta (input sequences)"]
        Results["Results/<br/>*.a3m (MSA outputs)"]
        Status["Status/<br/>*.status (job tracking)"]
        ServerLock["server.lock<br/>(server PID)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "MMseqs2 Server"
        ServerScript["mmseqs2_server_gpu.sh<br/>or mmseqs2_server_cpu.sh"]
        MMseqs2Bin["mmseqs binary<br/>easy-search or createdb"]
    end
    
    MMseqs2Tool -->|"generate_script()"| PipeMMseqs2
    PipeMMseqs2 -->|"Submit .fasta"| Queue
    PipeMMseqs2 -->|"Poll status"| Status
    Status -.->|"Monitor"| PipeMMseqs2
    
    ServerScript -->|"Watch"| Queue
    Queue -->|"Pick up jobs"| ServerScript
    ServerScript -->|"Run"| MMseqs2Bin
    MMseqs2Bin -->|"Write"| Results
    ServerScript -->|"Update"| Status
    
    Results -->|"Download when complete"| PipeMMseqs2
    
    PipeMMseqs2 -->|"Check server.lock"| ServerLock
    PipeMMseqs2 -->|"Auto-restart if dead"| ServerScript
```

**Sources:** High-level diagram (Diagram 5)

### Server Management

The client script automatically manages the server:

1. **Check server health:** Read `server.lock` for PID, verify process exists
2. **Start server if needed:** Submit SLURM job with `mmseqs2_server_gpu.sh`
3. **Submit jobs:** Write FASTA to `Queue/`
4. **Poll for completion:** Check `Status/*.status` files
5. **Download results:** Copy from `Results/*.a3m`

**Auto-restart logic:** If server PID is stale (process doesn't exist), client resubmits server job.

### MSA Masking

MMseqs2 tool supports masking specific regions during MSA search to prevent bias:

```python
from biopipelines.mmseqs2 import MMseqs2

# Mask designed regions (only search fixed scaffold)
msas = MMseqs2(
    sequences=designs,
    mask_regions=designs.tables.structures.designed  # Column reference
)
```

Masked regions are converted to 'X' during search, then restored in output MSAs.

### Output

- **DataStream:** `msas` (format: `"a3m"`, map_table: `"msas.csv"`)
- **TableInfo:** `msas.csv` with columns: `id`, `file`, `num_sequences`, `coverage`

**Sources:** High-level diagram (Diagram 5), MMseqs2 section

---

## Helper Script Patterns

All utility tools follow a common helper script pattern:

```mermaid
graph TB
    ToolClass["Tool class<br/>(e.g., PDB, Ligand)"]
    
    GenConfig["generate_script()<br/>Write config JSON"]
    GenBash["generate_script()<br/>Write bash wrapper"]
    
    ConfigJSON["config.json<br/>{ids, params, folders}"]
    BashScript["tool.sh<br/>Activate env + run helper"]
    
    HelperScript["pipe_*.py<br/>(e.g., pipe_pdb.py)"]
    
    ReadConfig["Read config JSON"]
    ProcessData["Process data<br/>(download, convert, extract)"]
    WriteOutputs["Write CSV tables + files"]
    
    ToolClass --> GenConfig
    ToolClass --> GenBash
    GenConfig --> ConfigJSON
    GenBash --> BashScript
    
    BashScript -->|"Execute"| HelperScript
    HelperScript --> ReadConfig
    ReadConfig --> ProcessData
    ProcessData --> WriteOutputs
    
    ConfigJSON -.->|"Read"| ReadConfig
```

**Configuration JSON** contains all parameters needed for execution (IDs, source paths, conversion settings, etc.)

**Bash wrapper** activates the appropriate conda/mamba environment and invokes the Python helper script.

**Helper script** reads config, performs the actual work (fetching, conversion, parsing), and writes standardized outputs.

**Sources:** HelpScripts/pipe_pdb.py:1445-1513, HelpScripts/pipe_ligand.py:1240-1320, HelpScripts/pipe_sequence.py:83-123

---

## Summary

Utility tools provide typed, reusable data input for BioPipelines workflows:

| Tool | Primary Purpose | Key Feature |
|------|-----------------|-------------|
| **PDB** | Fetch structures | Priority-based lookup, format conversion, operations |
| **RCSB** | Search & download | Advanced search API, typed attributes, query composition |
| **Ligand** | Fetch ligands | Multi-source lookup, SMILES→3D conversion, residue renaming |
| **Sequence** | Create sequences | Simple string→FASTA/CSV conversion |
| **CompoundLibrary** | Compound collections | Library support, property filtering |
| **Load/LoadMultiple** | Reuse outputs | Read previous pipeline results |
| **MMseqs2** | Generate MSAs | Client-server, GPU acceleration, masking |

All produce `StandardizedOutput` with typed streams and tables for seamless downstream integration.

---

# Structure Generation Tools

<details>

- [HelpScripts/pipe_ligand.py](HelpScripts/pipe_ligand.py)

This page documents the structure generation tools in BioPipelines: **RFdiffusion**, **RFdiffusion3**, **RFdiffusionAllAtom**, and **BoltzGen**. These tools generate novel protein backbones or complete binder structures, forming the foundation for computational protein design workflows.

For sequence design on existing backbones, see [Sequence Design Tools](#5.3). For structure prediction and validation, see [Structure Prediction Tools](#5.4) and [Analysis Tools](#5.5).

---

## Overview and Tool Ecosystem

Structure generation tools consume **input specifications** (contigs, hotspots, ligands) and produce **protein structures** (PDB/CIF files) with accompanying **metadata tables**. They are the primary entry point for de novo design pipelines.

**Tool Landscape:**

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Entities"
        Ligand["Ligand<br/>(CCD/PubChem/SMILES)"]
        PDB["PDB<br/>(templates/scaffolds)"]
        Sequence["Sequence<br/>(for inverse folding)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Structure Generation Tools"
        RFD["RFdiffusion<br/>Backbone generation"]
        RFD3["RFdiffusion3<br/>3rd-gen + ligands"]
        RFDAA["RFdiffusionAllAtom<br/>All-atom with ligands"]
        BoltzGen["BoltzGen<br/>End-to-end binder design"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Outputs"
        Structures["DataStream<br/>structures (PDB/CIF)"]
        Metrics["TableInfo<br/>metrics.csv"]
        Specs["TableInfo<br/>specifications.csv"]
        Sequences["DataStream<br/>sequences.fasta"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Downstream Tools"
        PMPNN["ProteinMPNN<br/>Sequence design"]
        LMPNN["LigandMPNN<br/>Ligand-aware design"]
        AF2["AlphaFold<br/>Structure prediction"]
        Boltz2["Boltz2<br/>Complex prediction"]
    end
    
    PDB --> RFD
    PDB --> RFD3
    Ligand --> RFD3
    Ligand --> RFDAA
    Ligand --> BoltzGen
    Sequence --> BoltzGen
    
    RFD --> Structures
    RFD3 --> Structures
    RFDAA --> Structures
    BoltzGen --> Structures
    BoltzGen --> Sequences
    
    RFD3 --> Metrics
    RFD3 --> Specs
    BoltzGen --> Metrics
    
    Structures --> PMPNN
    Structures --> LMPNN
    Sequences --> AF2
    Sequences --> Boltz2
```

**Sources:** [Docs/ToolReference.md:28-36](), [HelpScripts/pipe_rfdiffusion3_postprocess.py:1-25](), [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen.py:1-14]()
