# Page: Data Management Tools

# Data Management Tools

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [Docs/Tool/Analysis.md](Docs/Tool/Analysis.md)
- [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md](Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md)
- [Docs/ToolReference.md](Docs/ToolReference.md)
- [Docs/UserManual.md](Docs/UserManual.md)
- [config.yaml](config.yaml)

</details>



Data management tools enable transformation, filtering, and manipulation of tabular data and file collections produced by upstream tools in BioPipelines pipelines. These tools operate on `TableInfo` objects and `StandardizedOutput` containers, providing pandas-style operations, ID renaming, selection string manipulation, and metric export capabilities.

For information about input data loading (PDB, Ligand, Sequence), see [Utilities](#5.1). For structure and interaction analysis that produces tables, see [Analysis Tools](#5.5). For visualization of processed data, see [Visualization Tools](#5.7).

---

## Tool Overview

BioPipelines provides four primary data management tools:

| Tool | Primary Function | Input Types | Output Types |
|------|------------------|-------------|--------------|
| **Panda** | Table transformations (filter, sort, merge, calculate) | `TableInfo`, `StandardizedOutput` | `TableInfo`, optionally `DataStream` (pool mode) |
| **ReMap** | ID renaming across streams and tables | `StandardizedOutput` | All streams and tables with new IDs |
| **Selection** | PyMOL selection string manipulation | Column references with selection strings | `TableInfo` with modified selections |
| **ExtractMetrics** | Export metrics for statistical software | List of `TableInfo` | Separate CSV per metric |

All data management tools inherit from `BaseConfig` and use the `biopipelines` conda environment (or `ProteinEnv` for Selection). They follow the two-phase execution model: configuration phase predicts outputs and generates scripts, execution phase performs transformations.

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:1-247](), [Docs/UserManual.md:497-551]()

---

## Architecture Overview

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Sources"
        ToolOutput["StandardizedOutput<br/>from upstream tools"]
        TableInfo["TableInfo<br/>table metadata"]
        ColumnRef["Column References<br/>(TableInfo, column_name)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Management Tools"
        Panda["Panda<br/>biopipelines/panda.py<br/>filter, sort, merge,<br/>calculate, groupby"]
        ReMap["ReMap<br/>biopipelines/remap.py<br/>ID renaming"]
        Selection["Selection<br/>biopipelines/selection.py<br/>PyMOL selection ops"]
        ExtractMetrics["ExtractMetrics<br/>biopipelines/extract_metrics.py<br/>metric export"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Types"
        ResultTable["TableInfo<br/>tables.result"]
        MissingTable["TableInfo<br/>tables.missing"]
        PooledStreams["DataStream<br/>streams.structures<br/>streams.sequences"]
        RemappedStreams["DataStream<br/>new IDs"]
        RemappedTables["TableInfo<br/>new IDs"]
        SelectionTable["TableInfo<br/>tables.selections"]
        MetricTables["TableInfo<br/>per-metric CSVs"]
    end
    
    ToolOutput --> Panda
    TableInfo --> Panda
    ColumnRef --> Panda
    
    ToolOutput --> ReMap
    ColumnRef --> ReMap
    
    ColumnRef --> Selection
    ToolOutput --> Selection
    
    TableInfo --> ExtractMetrics
    
    Panda --> ResultTable
    Panda --> MissingTable
    Panda --> PooledStreams
    
    ReMap --> RemappedStreams
    ReMap --> RemappedTables
    
    Selection --> SelectionTable
    
    ExtractMetrics --> MetricTables
```

**Diagram: Data Management Tool Architecture**

This diagram shows the primary data management tools and their relationships to input/output types. `Panda` is the most versatile, accepting both tables and tool outputs with optional pooling. `ReMap` operates on complete tool outputs to rename IDs across all streams and tables. `Selection` manipulates PyMOL selection strings from column references. `ExtractMetrics` reorganizes metrics for statistical analysis.

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:1-247](), [config.yaml:106-109]()

---

## Panda: Unified Table Transformations

`Panda` provides pandas-style operations on CSV tables with optional file pooling. It replaces legacy tools (Filter, Rank, SelectBest, MergeTables, ConcatenateTables, SliceTable) with a unified operation-based interface.

### Core Class Structure

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Panda Class Hierarchy"
        BaseConfig["BaseConfig<br/>abstract base"]
        Panda["Panda<br/>biopipelines.panda<br/>class Panda(BaseConfig)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Operation Classes"
        Operation["Operation<br/>abstract base"]
        FilterOp["FilterOperation"]
        SortOp["SortOperation"]
        HeadOp["HeadOperation"]
        TailOp["TailOperation"]
        SampleOp["SampleOperation"]
        RankOp["RankOperation"]
        DropDuplicatesOp["DropDuplicatesOperation"]
        MergeOp["MergeOperation"]
        ConcatOp["ConcatOperation"]
        CalculateOp["CalculateOperation"]
        GroupByOp["GroupByOperation"]
        SelectColumnsOp["SelectColumnsOperation"]
        DropColumnsOp["DropColumnsOperation"]
        RenameOp["RenameOperation"]
        FillNaOp["FillNaOperation"]
        PivotOp["PivotOperation"]
        MeltOp["MeltOperation"]
        AverageBySourceOp["AverageBySourceOperation"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Helper Script"
        PipePanda["HelpScripts/pipe_panda.py<br/>execute transformations<br/>apply pooling<br/>write outputs"]
    end
    
    BaseConfig --> Panda
    Operation --> FilterOp
    Operation --> SortOp
    Operation --> HeadOp
    Operation --> TailOp
    Operation --> SampleOp
    Operation --> RankOp
    Operation --> DropDuplicatesOp
    Operation --> MergeOp
    Operation --> ConcatOp
    Operation --> CalculateOp
    Operation --> GroupByOp
    Operation --> SelectColumnsOp
    Operation --> DropColumnsOp
    Operation --> RenameOp
    Operation --> FillNaOp
    Operation --> PivotOp
    Operation --> MeltOp
    Operation --> AverageBySourceOp
    
    Panda --> PipePanda
```

**Diagram: Panda Class Structure and Operations**

The `Panda` class accepts operations as static factory methods (e.g., `Panda.filter()`, `Panda.sort()`), which return operation objects. These are serialized into JSON configuration and executed by `pipe_panda.py`.

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:7-118](), [Docs/UserManual.md:497-551]()

### Parameters and Modes

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `table` | `TableInfo` \| `StandardizedOutput` \| `str` | Single table input |
| `tables` | `List[TableInfo \| StandardizedOutput \| str]` | Multiple tables (for merge/concat) |
| `operations` | `List[Operation]` | Sequence of transformations to apply |
| `pool` | `StandardizedOutput` \| `List[StandardizedOutput]` | Copy files matching filtered IDs |
| `rename` | `str` | Rename output IDs to `{rename}_1`, `{rename}_2`, ... |

**Pool Mode**: When `pool` is provided, Panda copies files from the source tool's streams (structures, sequences, compounds) that match the filtered IDs. This enables workflows like "filter by confidence, keep matching structures."

**Rename Mode**: When `rename` is provided, output IDs are sequentially numbered regardless of source IDs. Combined with `pool`, this creates ranked file collections.

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:13-19]()

### Operations Reference

#### Single-Table Operations

| Operation | Signature | Description |
|-----------|-----------|-------------|
| `filter(expr)` | `Panda.filter("pLDDT > 80")` | Keep rows matching boolean expression |
| `sort(by, ascending)` | `Panda.sort("score", ascending=False)` | Sort by column |
| `head(n)` | `Panda.head(10)` | Keep first n rows |
| `tail(n)` | `Panda.tail(5)` | Keep last n rows |
| `sample(n, frac)` | `Panda.sample(n=100)` or `Panda.sample(frac=0.1)` | Random sample |
| `rank(by, prefix)` | `Panda.rank(by="score")` | Add rank column |
| `drop_duplicates(subset)` | `Panda.drop_duplicates(subset="sequence")` | Remove duplicate rows |

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:20-31]()

#### Multi-Table Operations

| Operation | Signature | Description |
|-----------|-----------|-------------|
| `merge(on, how, prefixes)` | `Panda.merge(prefixes=["a_", "b_"])` | Horizontal join (on="id" by default) |
| `concat(fill, add_source)` | `Panda.concat(fill="", add_source=True)` | Vertical stack |

**Merge behavior**: When `on=None` (default), uses BioPipelines ID matching. Prefixes are applied to all non-ID columns to avoid collisions.

**Concat behavior**: When `add_source=True`, adds a `source` column indicating which table each row came from. `fill` specifies default value for missing columns.

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:31-33]()

#### Column Operations

| Operation | Signature | Description |
|-----------|-----------|-------------|
| `calculate(exprs)` | `Panda.calculate({"delta": "a - b"})` | Add calculated columns |
| `select_columns(cols)` | `Panda.select_columns(["id", "score"])` | Keep only specified columns |
| `drop_columns(cols)` | `Panda.drop_columns(["temp"])` | Remove columns |
| `rename(mapping)` | `Panda.rename({"old": "new"})` | Rename columns |
| `fillna(value)` | `Panda.fillna(0)` | Fill missing values |

**Calculate expressions**: Support Python math operators (`+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `**`) and functions (`cos`, `sin`, `sqrt`, `log`, `exp`, `radians`, `degrees`, `pi`). Expressions can reference columns defined earlier in the same `calculate` call.

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:33-41]()

#### Reshaping Operations

| Operation | Signature | Description |
|-----------|-----------|-------------|
| `groupby(by, agg)` | `Panda.groupby("cat", {"score": "mean"})` | Group and aggregate |
| `pivot(index, columns, values)` | `Panda.pivot("id", "metric", "value")` | Pivot table |
| `melt(id_vars)` | `Panda.melt(id_vars="id")` | Unpivot table |
| `average_by_source()` | `Panda.average_by_source()` | Average across `source` column groups |

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:39-41]()

### Execution Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as "User Script"
    participant Panda as "Panda Class"
    participant BaseConfig as "BaseConfig"
    participant PipePanda as "HelpScripts/pipe_panda.py"
    
    rect rgb(230, 245, 255)
        Note over User,BaseConfig: Configuration Phase
        User->>Panda: Panda(tables=..., operations=[...], pool=...)
        Panda->>Panda: validate_params()
        Panda->>Panda: configure_inputs()
        Panda->>Panda: predict output IDs (if rename provided)
        Panda->>Panda: generate_script()
        Panda->>Panda: write config JSON
        Panda->>BaseConfig: auto-register
        BaseConfig->>User: return Panda instance
    end
    
    rect rgb(255, 245, 230)
        Note over PipePanda: Execution Phase (Bash)
        PipePanda->>PipePanda: load config JSON
        PipePanda->>PipePanda: read input tables as pandas DataFrames
        PipePanda->>PipePanda: apply operations sequentially
        
        alt pool mode
            PipePanda->>PipePanda: filter pool.streams by result IDs
            PipePanda->>PipePanda: copy/symlink matching files
            PipePanda->>PipePanda: update DataStream map_tables
        end
        
        alt rename mode
            PipePanda->>PipePanda: rename result IDs to {rename}_1, {rename}_2, ...
            PipePanda->>PipePanda: update all output CSVs with new IDs
        end
        
        PipePanda->>PipePanda: write result.csv
        PipePanda->>PipePanda: write missing.csv (pool mode)
        PipePanda->>PipePanda: create .completed marker
    end
```

**Diagram: Panda Execution Flow**

During configuration, `Panda` validates operations and predicts output structure. During execution, `pipe_panda.py` loads tables as pandas DataFrames, applies operations, and optionally pools files or renames IDs.

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:7-118](), [Docs/UserManual.md:1-611]()

### Common Usage Patterns

#### Filter and Pool

```python
from biopipelines.panda import Panda

# Filter high-confidence predictions and copy their structures
filtered = Panda(
    tables=boltz.tables.confidence,
    operations=[Panda.filter("pLDDT > 80")],
    pool=boltz
)
# Output: filtered.streams.structures (matching IDs only)
#         filtered.tables.result (filtered confidence.csv)
#         filtered.tables.missing (filtered out IDs)
```

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:49-58]()

#### Sort, Head, and Rename

```python
# Select top 5 by score and rename to "best_1", "best_2", etc.
best = Panda(
    tables=boltz.tables.confidence,
    operations=[
        Panda.sort("confidence_score", ascending=False),
        Panda.head(5)
    ],
    pool=boltz,
    rename="best"
)
# Output IDs: best_1, best_2, best_3, best_4, best_5
```

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:69-76]()

#### Merge and Calculate

```python
# Merge apo and holo affinity tables, calculate delta
merged = Panda(
    tables=[apo.tables.affinity, holo.tables.affinity],
    operations=[
        Panda.merge(prefixes=["apo_", "holo_"]),
        Panda.calculate({"delta": "holo_affinity - apo_affinity"})
    ]
)
# Result columns: id, apo_affinity, holo_affinity, delta
```

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:78-84]()

#### Complex Calculations

```python
# Calculate FRET efficiency from distance and orientation angle
# Math functions: cos, sin, sqrt, log, exp, radians, degrees, pi
fret = Panda(
    tables=[distances.tables.result, angles.tables.angles],
    operations=[
        Panda.merge(),
        Panda.calculate({
            "kappa2": "cos(orientation) ** 2",
            "R0_eff": "49.0 * (kappa2 / 0.6667) ** (1.0 / 6.0)",
            "efficiency": "1 / (1 + (distance / R0_eff) ** 6)"
        })
    ]
)
# Expressions can reference earlier-defined columns in same calculate call
```

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:86-99]()

#### Multi-Source Pooling

```python
# Select best structure from multiple design cycles
best = Panda(
    tables=[cycle1.tables.result, cycle2.tables.result],
    operations=[
        Panda.concat(add_source=True),
        Panda.sort("metric", ascending=True),
        Panda.head(1)
    ],
    pool=[cycle1, cycle2],  # Pool list matches tables list
    rename="best"
)
# Selects best structure across all cycles, renames to "best_1"
```

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:106-117]()

---

## ReMap: ID Management

`ReMap` renames IDs across all streams and tables from a source tool output. At execution time, files are symlinked (not copied) and CSV tables are rewritten with new IDs. This enables workflows where upstream IDs need to be aligned with a different ID scheme.

### Class Structure

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "ReMap Components"
        BaseConfig["BaseConfig<br/>abstract base"]
        ReMap["ReMap<br/>biopipelines.remap<br/>class ReMap(BaseConfig)"]
        PipeReMap["HelpScripts/pipe_remap.py<br/>symlink files<br/>rewrite CSVs<br/>update map_tables"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Input Types"
        Source["source: StandardizedOutput<br/>tool whose IDs will be renamed"]
        Onto["onto: str | list | dict |<br/>DataStream | StandardizedOutput"]
        Map["map: StandardizedOutput<br/>(optional provenance bridge)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        Streams["DataStream<br/>all source streams<br/>(where IDs match)"]
        Tables["TableInfo<br/>all source tables<br/>(with new IDs)"]
    end
    
    BaseConfig --> ReMap
    ReMap --> PipeReMap
    
    Source --> ReMap
    Onto --> ReMap
    Map --> ReMap
    
    ReMap --> Streams
    ReMap --> Tables
```

**Diagram: ReMap Architecture**

`ReMap` takes a `source` tool output and an `onto` specification. During execution, `pipe_remap.py` creates symlinks for all files and rewrites CSV tables with new IDs. Streams whose IDs cannot be fully remapped are discarded with a warning.

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:121-171]()

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `source` | `StandardizedOutput` | Tool output whose IDs will be renamed |
| `onto` | `str` \| `list` \| `dict` \| `list[tuple]` \| `DataStream` \| `StandardizedOutput` | Target ID specification (see table below) |
| `map` | `StandardizedOutput` (optional) | Intermediate tool for provenance bridging |

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:127-130]()

### `onto` Specification Modes

| Type | Behavior | Example |
|------|----------|---------|
| `str` | Auto-number with prefix | `"design"` → `design_1`, `design_2`, ... |
| `list[str]` | Explicit new IDs (matched by position) | `["kinase_apo", "kinase_holo"]` |
| `dict` | Selective mapping | `{"old_id": "new_id"}` |
| `list[tuple]` | Same as dict | `[("old_id", "new_id")]` |
| `DataStream` | Align onto stream's IDs | `tool_b.streams.structures` |
| `StandardizedOutput` | Align onto tool's IDs (all streams must share IDs) | `tool_b` |

**Auto-numbering**: When `onto` is a string, output IDs are `{onto}_1`, `{onto}_2`, etc., matching the order of source IDs.

**Alignment**: When `onto` is a `DataStream` or `StandardizedOutput`, ReMap attempts to match source IDs to target IDs. Unmatched IDs are dropped.

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:132-140]()

### Provenance Bridging with `map`

The optional `map` parameter enables ID remapping through an intermediate tool:

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["Tool A<br/>IDs: a1, a2, a3"]
    B["Tool B<br/>takes A as input<br/>IDs: b1, b2, b3"]
    C["Tool C<br/>takes B as input<br/>IDs: c1, c2, c3"]
    
    ReMap["ReMap<br/>source=A<br/>onto=C<br/>map=B"]
    
    A --> B
    B --> C
    A --> ReMap
    B -.provenance bridge.-> ReMap
    C --> ReMap
    
    ReMap --> Output["Output<br/>A's streams/tables<br/>with C's IDs"]
```

**Diagram: Provenance Bridging Pattern**

When Tool A produces outputs consumed by Tool B, which produces outputs consumed by Tool C, and you want to remap Tool A's IDs onto Tool C's IDs, use `ReMap(source=A, onto=C, map=B)`. ReMap traces provenance columns through B to establish A→C mapping.

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:127-171]()

### Usage Examples

#### Auto-Numbered Renaming

```python
from biopipelines.remap import ReMap

# Rename tool_a's IDs to "design_1", "design_2", ...
remapped = ReMap(source=tool_a, onto="design")
```

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:149-152]()

#### Explicit List Mapping

```python
# Rename two structures to specific IDs
remapped = ReMap(source=tool_a, onto=["kinase_apo", "kinase_holo"])
```

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:154-155]()

#### Dictionary Mapping

```python
# Selective renaming
remapped = ReMap(
    source=tool_a, 
    onto={"prot1": "complex_A", "prot2": "complex_B"}
)

# Or with list of tuples
remapped = ReMap(
    source=tool_a, 
    onto=[("prot1", "complex_A"), ("prot2", "complex_B")]
)
```

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:157-162]()

#### Alignment to Another Tool

```python
# Align tool_a's IDs onto tool_b's IDs
remapped = ReMap(source=tool_a, onto=tool_b)

# Or align onto a specific stream
remapped = ReMap(source=tool_a, onto=tool_b.streams.structures)
```

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:164-167]()

#### Provenance Bridging

```python
# Map tool_a onto tool_c through intermediate tool_b
remapped = ReMap(source=tool_a, onto=tool_c, map=tool_b)
```

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:169-171]()

---

## Selection: PyMOL Selection String Manipulation

`Selection` combines and modifies PyMOL-formatted selection strings using composable operations. This is useful for creating complex residue selections from multiple upstream analyses (e.g., "binding site residues, expanded by 2, excluding flexible regions").

### Class Structure

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Selection Components"
        BaseConfig["BaseConfig<br/>abstract base"]
        Selection["Selection<br/>biopipelines.selection<br/>class Selection(BaseConfig)"]
        SelectionOp["SelectionOp<br/>abstract operation base"]
        AddOp["AddOp: union"]
        SubtractOp["SubtractOp: difference"]
        ExpandOp["ExpandOp: add flanking residues"]
        ShrinkOp["ShrinkOp: remove flanking residues"]
        ShiftOp["ShiftOp: shift intervals"]
        InvertOp["InvertOp: complement"]
        PipeSelection["HelpScripts/pipe_selection.py<br/>parse selection strings<br/>apply operations<br/>generate output strings"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Input"
        ColumnRefs["Column References<br/>(TableInfo, column_name)"]
        Structures["structures: StandardizedOutput<br/>(for structure-aware ops)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        ResultTable["TableInfo<br/>tables.selections<br/>columns: id, pdb, {column},<br/>original_{column}"]
    end
    
    BaseConfig --> Selection
    SelectionOp --> AddOp
    SelectionOp --> SubtractOp
    SelectionOp --> ExpandOp
    SelectionOp --> ShrinkOp
    SelectionOp --> ShiftOp
    SelectionOp --> InvertOp
    
    Selection --> PipeSelection
    
    ColumnRefs --> Selection
    Structures --> Selection
    
    Selection --> ResultTable
```

**Diagram: Selection Tool Architecture**

`Selection` accepts a sequence of operations created by static factory methods (`Selection.add()`, `Selection.subtract()`, etc.). Each operation modifies the running selection. Structure-aware operations (expand, shrink, shift, invert) require the `structures` parameter to determine chain lengths.

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:203-246](), [config.yaml:109]()

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `*ops` | Sequence of `SelectionOp` | Operations to apply left-to-right |
| `structures` | `StandardizedOutput` (optional) | Required for structure-aware ops (expand, shrink, shift, invert) |

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:210-212]()

### Operations

| Operation | Description | Structure-Aware |
|-----------|-------------|-----------------|
| `Selection.add(*refs)` | Union of one or more column references | No |
| `Selection.subtract(*refs)` | Remove residues from running selection | No |
| `Selection.expand(n)` | Add n residues on each side | Yes |
| `Selection.shrink(n)` | Remove n residues from each side | Yes |
| `Selection.shift(n)` | Shift all intervals by n | Yes |
| `Selection.invert()` | Select complement | Yes |

**Selection string format**: PyMOL-style range notation (e.g., `"10-20+30-40"`) with `+` separating ranges.

**Structure-aware operations**: Require `structures` parameter because they need to know chain boundaries. For example, `invert()` needs to know the total chain length to compute the complement.

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:214-221]()

### Execution Pattern

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as "User Script"
    participant Selection as "Selection Class"
    participant PipeSelection as "HelpScripts/pipe_selection.py"
    
    rect rgb(230, 245, 255)
        Note over User,Selection: Configuration Phase
        User->>Selection: Selection(Selection.add(...), Selection.expand(2), ...)
        Selection->>Selection: validate ops
        Selection->>Selection: configure_inputs (resolve column refs)
        Selection->>Selection: generate_script()
        Selection->>Selection: write config JSON
        Selection->>User: return Selection instance
    end
    
    rect rgb(255, 245, 230)
        Note over PipeSelection: Execution Phase
        PipeSelection->>PipeSelection: load config JSON
        PipeSelection->>PipeSelection: read input table with selections
        PipeSelection->>PipeSelection: for each row (structure):
        PipeSelection->>PipeSelection: apply operations left-to-right
        PipeSelection->>PipeSelection: parse selection strings
        PipeSelection->>PipeSelection: add/subtract/expand/shrink/shift/invert
        PipeSelection->>PipeSelection: write output table with modified selections
        PipeSelection->>PipeSelection: create .completed marker
    end
```

**Diagram: Selection Execution Flow**

Operations are applied sequentially. For example, `Selection.add(col1, col2)` creates a union, then `Selection.expand(2)` adds 2 residues on each side, then `Selection.subtract(col3)` removes specified residues.

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:203-246]()

### Usage Examples

#### Expand Binding Site

```python
from biopipelines.selection import Selection
from biopipelines.distance_selector import DistanceSelector

# Find residues within 5Å of ligand
distances = DistanceSelector(structures=rfdaa, ligand="LIG", distance=5)

# Expand by 2 residues on each side
expanded = Selection(
    Selection.add(distances.tables.selections.within),
    Selection.expand(2),
    structures=rfdaa
)
# Output: distances.tables.selections.within expanded by 2 residues
```

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:227-238]()

#### Union and Invert

```python
from biopipelines.selection import Selection

# Union two regions (e.g., two linkers), then invert to get fixed positions
fixed = Selection(
    Selection.add(fuse.tables.sequences.L1, fuse.tables.sequences.L2),
    Selection.invert(),
    structures=fused_protein
)
# Output: complement of L1+L2 (i.e., everything except linkers)
```

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:240-246]()

#### Multi-Column Operations

```python
# Combine binding site, conserved regions, exclude flexible loops
design_positions = Selection(
    Selection.add(binding_site.tables.selections.within),  # Start with binding site
    Selection.expand(3),  # Add 3 residues around
    Selection.add(conserved.tables.selections.region),  # Add conserved region
    Selection.subtract(flexible.tables.selections.loops),  # Remove flexible loops
    structures=protein
)
```

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:203-246]()

---

## ExtractMetrics: Statistical Software Export

`ExtractMetrics` reorganizes tabular data into a format suitable for statistical software like GraphPad Prism. It creates one CSV file per metric, with columns representing different experimental conditions.

### Class Structure

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "ExtractMetrics Components"
        BaseConfig["BaseConfig<br/>abstract base"]
        ExtractMetrics["ExtractMetrics<br/>biopipelines.extract_metrics<br/>class ExtractMetrics(BaseConfig)"]
        PipeExtractMetrics["HelpScripts/pipe_extract_metrics.py<br/>read input tables<br/>extract metric columns<br/>write per-metric CSVs"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Input"
        Tables["tables: List[TableInfo | str]<br/>one per condition"]
        Metrics["metrics: List[str]<br/>column names to extract"]
        TableNames["table_names: List[str]<br/>(optional) custom column names"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        MetricFiles["TableInfo per metric<br/>tables.{metric_name}<br/>columns: condition1, condition2, ..."]
    end
    
    BaseConfig --> ExtractMetrics
    ExtractMetrics --> PipeExtractMetrics
    
    Tables --> ExtractMetrics
    Metrics --> ExtractMetrics
    TableNames --> ExtractMetrics
    
    ExtractMetrics --> MetricFiles
```

**Diagram: ExtractMetrics Architecture**

`ExtractMetrics` takes multiple tables (one per experimental condition) and extracts specified metric columns. Each metric becomes a separate CSV file with conditions as columns.

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:175-200](), [config.yaml:108]()

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `tables` | `List[TableInfo \| str]` | Input tables (one per condition) |
| `metrics` | `List[str]` | Column names to extract |
| `table_names` | `List[str]` (optional) | Custom column names for output CSVs (default: table_1, table_2, ...) |

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:180-184]()

### Output Format

For each metric in `metrics`, `ExtractMetrics` creates a table with:
- Rows: one per unique ID across all input tables
- Columns: one per input table (named by `table_names` if provided, otherwise `table_1`, `table_2`, ...)

**Example transformation**:

Input tables (3 conditions):
```
# cycle0_affinity.csv
id,affinity
prot1,-8.5
prot2,-7.2

# cycle1_affinity.csv
id,affinity
prot1,-9.1
prot2,-7.8

# cycle2_affinity.csv
id,affinity
prot1,-9.5
prot2,-8.0
```

Output (affinity.csv):
```
id,Cycle0,Cycle1,Cycle2
prot1,-8.5,-9.1,-9.5
prot2,-7.2,-7.8,-8.0
```

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:186-188]()

### Usage Example

```python
from biopipelines.extract_metrics import ExtractMetrics

# Extract affinity and pLDDT metrics from three design cycles
metrics = ExtractMetrics(
    tables=[
        cycle0.tables.merged, 
        cycle1.tables.merged, 
        cycle2.tables.merged
    ],
    metrics=["affinity_delta", "pLDDT"],
    table_names=["Cycle0", "Cycle1", "Cycle2"]
)
# Output: 
#   metrics.tables.affinity_delta (path: affinity_delta.csv)
#   metrics.tables.pLDDT (path: pLDDT.csv)
```

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:190-200]()

---

## Data Transformation Workflows

### Typical Data Management Patterns

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Pattern 1: Filter and Pool"
        A1["Upstream Tool<br/>generates structures + metrics"]
        A2["Panda<br/>filter(metric > threshold)"]
        A3["Output<br/>filtered structures"]
        A1 --> A2
        A2 --> A3
    end
    
    subgraph "Pattern 2: Merge and Calculate"
        B1["Tool A<br/>affinity metrics"]
        B2["Tool B<br/>confidence metrics"]
        B3["Panda<br/>merge + calculate"]
        B4["Output<br/>combined metrics"]
        B1 --> B3
        B2 --> B3
        B3 --> B4
    end
    
    subgraph "Pattern 3: Rank and Rename"
        C1["Upstream Tool<br/>scored structures"]
        C2["Panda<br/>sort + head + rename"]
        C3["Output<br/>top_1, top_2, top_3, ..."]
        C1 --> C2
        C2 --> C3
    end
    
    subgraph "Pattern 4: Selection Manipulation"
        D1["DistanceSelector<br/>binding site"]
        D2["Selection<br/>expand + subtract"]
        D3["Downstream Design Tool<br/>redesigned positions"]
        D1 --> D2
        D2 --> D3
    end
    
    subgraph "Pattern 5: ID Alignment"
        E1["Design Tool<br/>IDs: design_1, design_2, ..."]
        E2["Prediction Tool<br/>IDs: pred_1, pred_2, ..."]
        E3["ReMap<br/>align IDs"]
        E4["Downstream Analysis<br/>matched IDs"]
        E1 --> E3
        E2 --> E3
        E3 --> E4
    end
```

**Diagram: Common Data Management Workflow Patterns**

These five patterns represent the most common use cases for data management tools in BioPipelines. Pattern 1 filters results and pools matching files. Pattern 2 merges metrics from different tools. Pattern 3 ranks and renames for clarity. Pattern 4 manipulates residue selections for design. Pattern 5 aligns ID schemes across tools.

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:1-247](), [Docs/UserManual.md:497-551]()

### Multi-Cycle Design Workflow

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Cycle 0: Initial Design"
        C0_Design["Design Tool<br/>100 sequences"]
        C0_Predict["Prediction Tool<br/>100 structures"]
        C0_Filter["Panda<br/>filter top 20%<br/>pool structures"]
        
        C0_Design --> C0_Predict
        C0_Predict --> C0_Filter
    end
    
    subgraph "Cycle 1: Refinement"
        C1_Design["Design Tool<br/>takes C0 structures<br/>100 new sequences"]
        C1_Predict["Prediction Tool<br/>100 structures"]
        C1_Filter["Panda<br/>filter top 20%<br/>pool structures"]
        
        C0_Filter --> C1_Design
        C1_Design --> C1_Predict
        C1_Predict --> C1_Filter
    end
    
    subgraph "Cycle 2: Final Selection"
        C2_Design["Design Tool<br/>takes C1 structures<br/>100 new sequences"]
        C2_Predict["Prediction Tool<br/>100 structures"]
        C2_Filter["Panda<br/>filter top 20%<br/>pool structures"]
        
        C1_Filter --> C2_Design
        C2_Design --> C2_Predict
        C2_Predict --> C2_Filter
    end
    
    subgraph "Final Analysis"
        Concat["Panda<br/>concat all cycles<br/>add_source=True"]
        Final["Panda<br/>sort + head<br/>rename='final'<br/>pool=[C0, C1, C2]"]
        Export["ExtractMetrics<br/>per-cycle comparison"]
        
        C0_Filter --> Concat
        C1_Filter --> Concat
        C2_Filter --> Concat
        
        Concat --> Final
        Concat --> Export
    end
```

**Diagram: Multi-Cycle Design with Data Management**

This workflow demonstrates how Panda enables iterative design refinement. Each cycle filters the top performers and pools their structures for the next cycle. Final analysis concatenates all cycles, selects the global best, and exports metrics for statistical comparison.

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:49-117](), [Docs/UserManual.md:497-551]()

---

## Integration with Other Tools

### Data Management in Analysis Workflows

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Structure Generation"
        RFdiff["RFdiffusion<br/>backbones"]
        MPNN["ProteinMPNN<br/>sequences"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Prediction"
        AF["AlphaFold<br/>structures + confidence"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Analysis"
        Distance["Distance<br/>binding site metrics"]
        Contacts["Contacts<br/>interaction counts"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Management"
        Merge["Panda<br/>merge confidence + distance + contacts"]
        Filter["Panda<br/>filter(pLDDT > 80 & contacts > 5)"]
        Pool["Panda<br/>pool matching structures"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Visualization"
        PyMOL["PyMOL<br/>create sessions"]
        Plot["Plot<br/>scatter plots"]
    end
    
    RFdiff --> MPNN
    MPNN --> AF
    AF --> Distance
    AF --> Contacts
    
    AF --> Merge
    Distance --> Merge
    Contacts --> Merge
    
    Merge --> Filter
    Filter --> Pool
    
    Pool --> PyMOL
    Pool --> Plot
```

**Diagram: Data Management in Analysis Workflows**

Data management tools serve as a bridge between analysis and visualization. `Panda` merges metrics from multiple analysis tools, filters based on combined criteria, and pools matching structures for visualization.

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:1-247](), [Docs/Tool/Analysis.md:1-458]()

### Column References and Metadata Propagation

Data management tools extensively use **column references** to pass metadata between tools. A column reference is a tuple `(TableInfo, "column_name")` that enables dynamic parameter resolution at execution time.

```python
from biopipelines.rfdiffusion import RFdiffusion
from biopipelines.ligandmpnn import LigandMPNN
from biopipelines.panda import Panda

# RFdiffusion outputs table with 'designed' column
rfd = RFdiffusion(contigs="50-100", num_designs=5)

# Use column reference for per-structure designed positions
lmpnn = LigandMPNN(
    structures=rfd,
    ligand="LIG",
    redesigned=rfd.tables.structures.designed  # Column reference
)

# Filter by confidence, pool structures
filtered = Panda(
    tables=lmpnn.tables.confidence,
    operations=[Panda.filter("confidence_score > 0.8")],
    pool=lmpnn
)

# Use filtered results for downstream design
# Selection tool can reference filtered table columns
from biopipelines.selection import Selection
expanded = Selection(
    Selection.add(filtered.tables.result.designed_positions),
    Selection.expand(2),
    structures=filtered
)
```

For more information on column references and how they enable metadata-driven parameterization, see [Table Column References and Metadata Propagation](#7.4).

**Sources:** [Docs/UserManual.md:373-392](), [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:1-247]()

---

## Environment and Dependencies

All data management tools use the `biopipelines` conda environment except `Selection`, which uses `ProteinEnv` (for PyMOL-based selection parsing).

| Tool | Environment | Key Dependencies |
|------|-------------|------------------|
| `Panda` | `biopipelines` | pandas, numpy |
| `ReMap` | `biopipelines` | pandas |
| `Selection` | `ProteinEnv` | pymol (via PyMOL environment) |
| `ExtractMetrics` | `biopipelines` | pandas |

**Sources:** [config.yaml:106-109](), [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:11-179-208]()

---

## Summary

Data management tools provide the glue between computational stages in BioPipelines workflows:

- **Panda**: Unified table transformations with optional file pooling, enabling filter-pool-redesign cycles
- **ReMap**: ID alignment across tool outputs, critical for provenance tracking and multi-tool comparisons
- **Selection**: Composable residue selection manipulation, bridging structural analysis and design
- **ExtractMetrics**: Export to statistical software for publication-ready analysis

All tools follow the two-phase execution model, use JSON configuration files, and integrate seamlessly with other BioPipelines tools through `StandardizedOutput` and column references.

**Sources:** [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md:1-247](), [Docs/UserManual.md:1-611]()

---

# Page: Visualization Tools

# Visualization Tools

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [Docs/Tool/Analysis.md](Docs/Tool/Analysis.md)
- [Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md](Docs/Tool/DataManagement.md)
- [Docs/ToolReference.md](Docs/ToolReference.md)
- [HelpScripts/pipe_plot.py](HelpScripts/pipe_plot.py)
- [biopipelines/base_config.py](biopipelines/base_config.py)
- [biopipelines/plot.py](biopipelines/plot.py)
- [biopipelines/pymol.py](biopipelines/pymol.py)

</details>



BioPipelines provides two visualization tools for creating publication-quality figures and interactive structure sessions: **PyMOL** for structure visualization and **Plot** for data plotting. Both tools use a declarative operation-based API that separates visualization logic from execution, enabling reproducible graphics generation across different environments.

For data transformation before visualization, see [Data Management Tools](#5.6). For analysis tools that generate metrics to visualize, see [Analysis Tools](#5.5).

---

## Overview of Visualization Architecture

Both PyMOL and Plot follow the same design pattern:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Configuration Phase (Python)"
        UserCode[User Pipeline Script]
        Tool[PyMOL or Plot Tool]
        Operations[Operation Sequence]
        Config[JSON Configuration File]
    end
    
    subgraph "Execution Phase (Bash)"
        Helper[Helper Script<br/>pipe_pymol.py or pipe_plot.py]
        Builder[Operation Builder<br/>PyMOLBuilder or PlotBuilder]
        Output[PNG Images<br/>PSE Sessions<br/>CSV Data]
    end
    
    UserCode --> Tool
    Tool --> Operations
    Operations --> Config
    Config --> Helper
    Helper --> Builder
    Builder --> Output
    
    style Tool fill:#e1f5ff
    style Builder fill:#ffe1e1
```

**Key Characteristics:**
1. **Declarative API**: Users specify *what* to visualize, not *how* to execute it
2. **Operation Sequencing**: Visualizations are built as a sequence of composable operations
3. **Data Source Abstraction**: Operations reference `StandardizedOutput` or `TableInfo` objects without file paths
4. **Config-Driven Execution**: Python generates JSON configs; bash scripts execute via helper scripts
5. **Dual Output**: Images (PNG) and session files (PSE) or data tables (CSV)

Sources: [biopipelines/pymol.py:1-786](), [biopipelines/plot.py:1-642]()

---

## PyMOL Tool

The `PyMOL` tool creates PyMOL sessions (`.pse`) and renders structure images (`.png`) using a sequence of declarative operations. It supports ID-based matching between structures and table columns for per-structure selections and naming.

### PyMOL Class Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "PyMOL Class (BaseConfig)"
        Init["__init__(*operations, session='session')"]
        StaticOps[Static Operation Factories<br/>Names, Load, Color, Align, etc.]
        Methods[Instance Methods<br/>validate_params()<br/>configure_inputs()<br/>generate_script()<br/>get_output_files()]
    end
    
    subgraph "PyMOLOperation Objects"
        OpNames["PyMOLOperation('names')"]
        OpLoad["PyMOLOperation('load')"]
        OpColor["PyMOLOperation('color')"]
        OpAlign["PyMOLOperation('align')"]
        OpRender["PyMOLOperation('render_each')"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Outputs"
        Session[".pse Session File"]
        Renders["DataStream (renders)"]
        PNG["PNG Image Files"]
    end
    
    Init --> OpNames
    Init --> OpLoad
    Init --> OpColor
    Init --> OpAlign
    Init --> OpRender
    
    StaticOps --> OpNames
    StaticOps --> OpLoad
    
    Methods --> Session
    Methods --> Renders
    Renders --> PNG
    
    style Init fill:#e1f5ff
    style Session fill:#ffe1e1
```

Sources: [biopipelines/pymol.py:41-95](), [biopipelines/pymol.py:503-525]()

### Available PyMOL Operations

The `PyMOL` class provides static factory methods for creating operations:

| Operation | Purpose | Key Parameters |
|-----------|---------|----------------|
| `Names(prefix, basename, suffix)` | Map IDs to PyMOL object names | `basename`: table column for variable part |
| `Load(structures)` | Load structures into session | `structures`: StandardizedOutput or DataStream |
| `Color(color, structures, selection)` | Color structures or selections | `selection`: table column or string |
| `ColorAF(structures, upper)` | Color by pLDDT (B-factor) | `upper`: max B-factor (1 for Boltz2, 100 for AF2) |
| `ColorAlign(reference, targets, ...)` | Color by sequence alignment | Shows identical/similar/different residues |
| `Align(method, target, selection)` | Align structures | `method`: "align", "super", "cealign" |
| `Show(structures, representation, selection)` | Show representation | `representation`: "cartoon", "sticks", etc. |
| `Hide(structures, representation, selection)` | Hide representation | `representation`: "everything", "cartoon", etc. |
| `Set(setting, value, selection)` | Set PyMOL setting | Any PyMOL setting |
| `Center(selection)` | Center view without rotation | |
| `Zoom(selection, buffer)` | Zoom to fit selection | `buffer`: extra space in Å |
| `Orient(selection)` | Orient view by principal axes | |
| `Ray(width, height)` | Ray trace current view | Dimensions in pixels |
| `PNG(filename, width, height, ray, dpi)` | Save PNG image | `filename`: supports `{id}` placeholder |
| `Render(structures, ...)` | Single rendered image | Orients and ray traces |
| `RenderEach(structures, ...)` | Render each structure separately | Creates multiple PNGs |

Sources: [biopipelines/pymol.py:136-500]()

### PyMOL Operation Execution Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant PyMOL as PyMOL Tool
    participant Config as pymol_config.json
    participant Helper as pipe_pymol.py
    participant Session as PyMOL Session
    
    User->>PyMOL: PyMOL(Names(...), Load(...), Color(...), ...)
    PyMOL->>PyMOL: Extract structure sources
    PyMOL->>PyMOL: Extract table references
    PyMOL->>PyMOL: validate_params()
    
    Note over PyMOL: Configuration Phase
    PyMOL->>Config: Serialize operations to JSON
    PyMOL->>Config: Save DataStreams as separate JSONs
    PyMOL->>Config: Save table column references
    
    Note over Helper: Execution Phase (Bash)
    Helper->>Config: Load operation sequence
    Helper->>Helper: Load structures by ID
    Helper->>Helper: Resolve table columns per-ID
    Helper->>Helper: Execute operations in order
    Helper->>Session: Save .pse session file
    Helper->>Session: Save PNG renders
```

Sources: [biopipelines/pymol.py:576-691](), [biopipelines/pymol.py:659-691]()

### ID-Based Matching and Table References

PyMOL supports **per-structure selections** using table column references. When a table column is passed as a `selection` parameter, PyMOL looks up the value for each structure's ID:

**Example:**
```python
# fuse.tables.sequences has columns: id | D1 | L1 | D2 | lengths
# D1="1-50", L1="51-60", D2="61-120" for each structure

PyMOL(
    PyMOL.Names(prefix="sensor", basename=fuse.tables.sequences.lengths, suffix="parts"),
    PyMOL.Load(fused_structures),
    PyMOL.Color("marine", selection=fuse.tables.sequences.D1),   # Per-structure D1 selection
    PyMOL.Color("gray50", selection=fuse.tables.sequences.L1),   # Per-structure L1 selection
    PyMOL.Color("white", selection=fuse.tables.sequences.D2),    # Per-structure D2 selection
    PyMOL.Align(selection=fuse.tables.sequences.D2),             # Align only on D2
)
```

**Table Column Resolution:**
- `fuse.tables.sequences.D1` creates a `TableReference(path, "D1")`
- Serialized to JSON as `{"type": "table_column", "table_path": "...", "column_name": "D1"}`
- Helper script reads CSV, looks up `D1` value for each structure ID
- Applied as PyMOL selection: `select domain1, {object_name} and resi {D1_value}`

Sources: [biopipelines/pymol.py:174-196](), [biopipelines/pymol.py:590-657]()

### PyMOL Output Structure

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "PyMOL Outputs"
        Session[session.pse<br/>PyMOL Session File]
        
        Renders[renders DataStream]
        
        PNG1[render1.png]
        PNG2[render2.png]
        PNGn[...]
    end
    
    Renders --> PNG1
    Renders --> PNG2
    Renders --> PNGn
    
    style Session fill:#fff4e1
    style Renders fill:#e1ffe1
```

**Output Files:**
- **Session File**: `.pse` file containing all loaded structures, colors, alignments
- **Renders DataStream**: PNG images from `Render`, `RenderEach`, or `PNG` operations
  - IDs: structure IDs or custom names
  - Files: PNG file paths
  - Format: "png"

Sources: [biopipelines/pymol.py:692-753]()

### PyMOL Configuration Example

```python
from biopipelines.pymol import PyMOL

# Color protein by pLDDT, ligand by atom, orient on ligand, render each
viz = PyMOL(
    PyMOL.RenderEach(
        structures=boltz_predictions,
        orient_selection="resn LIG",
        color_protein="plddt",
        color_ligand="byatom",
        ligand_selection="resn LIG",
        plddt_upper=1,  # Boltz2 uses 0-1 confidence
        width=1920,
        height=1080
    )
)

# Multi-structure session with alignment coloring
viz = PyMOL(
    PyMOL.Load(reference),
    PyMOL.Load(designs),
    PyMOL.ColorAlign(
        reference=reference,
        targets=designs,
        identical="white",
        similar="wheat",
        different="salmon",
        notcovered="gray50"
    ),
    PyMOL.Align(method="super"),
    PyMOL.Save("alignment.pse")
)
```

Sources: [biopipelines/pymol.py:49-61](), [Docs/Tool/Utilities.md:23-24]()

## Plot Tool

The `Plot` tool creates data visualizations from CSV tables using matplotlib and seaborn. It supports scatter plots, histograms, bar charts, column plots (Prism-style), and heatmaps.

### Plot Class Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Plot Class (BaseConfig)"
        Init["__init__(*operations)"]
        StaticOps[Static Operation Factories<br/>Scatter, Histogram, Bar, Column, HeatMap]
        Methods[Instance Methods<br/>validate_params()<br/>configure_inputs()<br/>generate_script()<br/>get_output_files()]
    end
    
    subgraph "PlotOperation Objects"
        OpScatter["PlotOperation('scatter')"]
        OpHist["PlotOperation('histogram')"]
        OpBar["PlotOperation('bar')"]
        OpCol["PlotOperation('column')"]
        OpHeat["PlotOperation('heatmap')"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Outputs"
        Plots["DataStream (plots)"]
        PNG["PNG Image Files"]
        CSV["CSV Data Exports"]
        Metadata["metadata.csv Table"]
    end
    
    Init --> OpScatter
    Init --> OpHist
    Init --> OpBar
    Init --> OpCol
    Init --> OpHeat
    
    StaticOps --> OpScatter
    
    Methods --> Plots
    Methods --> Metadata
    Plots --> PNG
    PNG --> CSV
    
    style Init fill:#e1f5ff
    style Plots fill:#ffe1e1
```

Sources: [biopipelines/plot.py:41-96](), [biopipelines/plot.py:362-383]()

### Available Plot Operations

| Operation | Purpose | Required Parameters | Optional Parameters |
|-----------|---------|---------------------|---------------------|
| `Scatter(data, x, y)` | X vs Y scatter plot | `x`, `y`: column names | `color`: grouping column<br/>`title`, `xlabel`, `ylabel`<br/>`figsize`, `dpi`<br/>`x_tick_rotation`, `grid`<br/>`color_legend_loc`, `color_legend_outside` |
| `Histogram(data, x)` | Distribution histogram | `x`: column name | `bins`: number of bins<br/>`title`, `xlabel`, `ylabel`<br/>`figsize`, `dpi` |
| `Bar(data, x, y)` | Categorical bar chart | `x`: categories, `y`: values | `y_right`: secondary Y axis<br/>`title`, `xlabel`, `ylabel`, `ylabel_right`<br/>`color_left`, `color_right`<br/>`figsize`, `dpi`<br/>`x_tick_rotation`, `grid`<br/>`legend_loc`, `legend_outside` |
| `Column(data, y)` | Multi-source comparison | `data`: list of sources, `y`: column | `labels`: x-axis labels<br/>`style`: "column", "simple_bar", "scatter", "box", "floating_bar"<br/>`show_error`: "sd", "sem", "ci"<br/>`color_groups`, `colors`<br/>`color_legend_title`, `color_legend_loc`, `color_legend_outside`<br/>`figsize`, `dpi`, `grid` |
| `HeatMap(data, ...)` | Heatmap matrix | **Pivot mode**: `x`, `y`, `value`<br/>**Correlation mode**: `columns` | `title`, `xlabel`, `ylabel`<br/>`cmap`, `annotate`<br/>`figsize`, `dpi` |

Sources: [biopipelines/plot.py:104-359]()

### Plot Operation Execution Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Plot as Plot Tool
    participant Config as plot_config.json
    participant Helper as pipe_plot.py
    participant Builder as PlotBuilder
    participant Output as PNG + CSV
    
    User->>Plot: Plot(Scatter(...), Histogram(...), ...)
    Plot->>Plot: Extract data sources
    Plot->>Plot: validate_params()
    
    Note over Plot: Configuration Phase
    Plot->>Config: Serialize operations to JSON
    Plot->>Config: Serialize table references
    Plot->>Config: Generate plot filenames
    
    Note over Helper: Execution Phase (Bash)
    Helper->>Config: Load configuration
    Helper->>Builder: PlotBuilder(config)
    
    loop Each Operation
        Builder->>Builder: Load data from CSV
        Builder->>Builder: Execute plot type (scatter, histogram, etc.)
        Builder->>Output: Save PNG image
        Builder->>Output: Export CSV data
        Builder->>Builder: Record metadata
    end
    
    Builder->>Output: Write metadata.csv
```

Sources: [biopipelines/plot.py:398-430](), [biopipelines/plot.py:533-563](), [HelpScripts/pipe_plot.py:33-95]()

### Data Source Resolution

Plot operations accept multiple data source types:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Data Source Types"
        TableInfo[TableInfo Object<br/>tool.tables.result]
        StdOutput[StandardizedOutput<br/>tool with .tables attribute]
        StrPath[String Path<br/>'path/to/file.csv']
    end
    
    subgraph "Resolution Process"
        Serialize[_serialize_data_source]
        JSON[JSON Config Entry]
    end
    
    subgraph "Helper Script"
        Load[_resolve_data_source]
        DataFrame[pandas DataFrame]
    end
    
    TableInfo --> Serialize
    StdOutput --> Serialize
    StrPath --> Serialize
    
    Serialize --> JSON
    JSON --> Load
    Load --> DataFrame
    
    style JSON fill:#fff4e1
```

**Serialization:**
- **TableInfo**: `{"type": "table_info", "path": "...", "name": "..."}`
- **StandardizedOutput**: Extracts first table, saves as `{"type": "standardized_output", "path": "...", "name": "...", "output_folder": "..."}`
- **String**: Direct path string

Sources: [biopipelines/plot.py:482-501](), [HelpScripts/pipe_plot.py:50-73]()

### Plot Output Structure

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Plot Outputs"
        Plots[plots DataStream]
        
        PNG1[plot1.png]
        PNG2[plot2.png]
        PNGn[...]
        
        CSV1[plot1.csv]
        CSV2[plot2.csv]
        CSVn[...]
        
        Metadata[metadata.csv]
    end
    
    Plots --> PNG1
    Plots --> PNG2
    Plots --> PNGn
    
    PNG1 -.exports data.-> CSV1
    PNG2 -.exports data.-> CSV2
    PNGn -.exports data.-> CSVn
    
    style Plots fill:#e1ffe1
    style Metadata fill:#fff4e1
```

**Output Files:**
- **plots DataStream**: PNG image files
  - IDs: "plot_1", "plot_2", ...
  - Files: PNG file paths (generated from title or operation type)
  - Format: "png"
- **Tables**: 
  - `metadata`: Summary CSV with columns `[filename, type, title, x_column, y_column, data_sources]`
  - `{plot_name}`: Data CSV for each plot (same name as PNG without extension)

Sources: [biopipelines/plot.py:565-610](), [HelpScripts/pipe_plot.py:191-208]()

### Plot Helper Script Operations

The `pipe_plot.py` helper script implements plot generation using `PlotBuilder`:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "PlotBuilder Methods"
        Scatter["execute_scatter()<br/>X vs Y with optional color groups"]
        Hist["execute_histogram()<br/>Distribution with stats annotation"]
        Bar["execute_bar()<br/>Categorical bars<br/>Optional dual Y-axis"]
        Column["execute_column()<br/>Multi-source comparison<br/>Styles: column, simple_bar, scatter, box, floating_bar"]
        Heatmap["execute_heatmap()<br/>Pivot or correlation matrix"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Common Steps"
        Load[Load CSV with fillna]
        Style[Apply matplotlib styling]
        Export[Export PNG + CSV]
        Meta[Record metadata]
    end
    
    Scatter --> Load
    Hist --> Load
    Bar --> Load
    Column --> Load
    Heatmap --> Load
    
    Load --> Style
    Style --> Export
    Export --> Meta
    
    style Export fill:#ffe1e1
```

**Key Features:**
1. **Automatic styling**: Consistent whitegrid theme, spines removed, grid control
2. **Data export**: Every plot saves both PNG and CSV with plot data
3. **Metadata tracking**: Aggregates plot info into metadata.csv
4. **Label resolution**: Uses `xlabel` > `x_name` > column name for axis labels
5. **Error handling**: NaN handling for string columns, validation of column existence

Sources: [HelpScripts/pipe_plot.py:128-716]()

### Plot Configuration Examples

```python
from biopipelines.plot import Plot

# Single scatter plot with color grouping
Plot(
    Plot.Scatter(
        data=analysis.tables.results,
        x="pLDDT",
        y="affinity",
        color="source",
        title="pLDDT vs Affinity by Source",
        color_legend_outside=True
    )
)

# Multi-plot comparison
Plot(
    Plot.Histogram(data=cycle0, x="pLDDT", bins=30, title="Cycle 0"),
    Plot.Histogram(data=cycle1, x="pLDDT", bins=30, title="Cycle 1"),
    Plot.Histogram(data=cycle2, x="pLDDT", bins=30, title="Cycle 2"),
)

# Column plot (Prism-style) with color groups
Plot(
    Plot.Column(
        data=[apo.tables.results, holo.tables.results, mutant.tables.results],
        y="affinity",
        labels=["Apo", "Holo", "Mutant"],
        style="column",
        show_error="sd",
        color_groups=["WT", "WT", "Mutant"],
        colors=["#1f77b4", "#1f77b4", "#ff7f0e"],
        color_legend_title="Variant",
        title="Affinity Comparison"
    )
)

# Correlation heatmap
Plot(
    Plot.HeatMap(
        data=analysis.tables.merged,
        columns=["pLDDT", "affinity", "contacts", "RMSD"],
        title="Metric Correlations",
        annotate=True
    )
)

# Dual Y-axis bar chart
Plot(
    Plot.Bar(
        data=results,
        x="condition",
        y="affinity",
        y_right="pLDDT",
        ylabel="Affinity (nM)",
        ylabel_right="pLDDT",
        title="Affinity and Confidence by Condition",
        legend_outside=True
    )
)
```

Sources: [biopipelines/plot.py:49-85](), [Docs/Tool/Utilities.md:23-24]()

---

## Helper Script Execution Model

Both PyMOL and Plot follow the same two-phase execution pattern:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Configuration Phase (Python)"
        Tool[Tool.__init__<br/>operations=...]
        Validate[validate_params]
        SerializeOps[Serialize operations to JSON]
        SerializeData[Serialize data sources<br/>DataStreams, TableInfo]
        WriteConfig[Write config.json]
        GenScript[generate_script<br/>Bash wrapper]
    end
    
    subgraph "Execution Phase (Bash)"
        ActivateEnv[Activate environment<br/>biopipelines or ProteinEnv]
        RunHelper[python pipe_*.py --config config.json]
        LoadConfig[Load JSON config]
        ResolveData[Resolve data sources<br/>Load CSVs, DataStreams]
        ExecuteOps[Execute operations in sequence]
        WriteOutput[Write PNG, PSE, CSV files]
        Completion[Create completion marker]
    end
    
    Tool --> Validate
    Validate --> SerializeOps
    SerializeOps --> SerializeData
    SerializeData --> WriteConfig
    WriteConfig --> GenScript
    
    GenScript -.bash execution.-> ActivateEnv
    ActivateEnv --> RunHelper
    RunHelper --> LoadConfig
    LoadConfig --> ResolveData
    ResolveData --> ExecuteOps
    ExecuteOps --> WriteOutput
    WriteOutput --> Completion
    
    style WriteConfig fill:#fff4e1
    style WriteOutput fill:#ffe1e1
```

**Configuration Phase Steps:**
1. User creates tool with operation sequence
2. Tool extracts dependencies (structure sources, table references)
3. Operations serialized to JSON with data source metadata
4. DataStreams saved as separate JSON files
5. Table references converted to `{table_path, column_name}` dicts
6. Config file written to `output_folder/config.json`
7. Bash script generated with environment activation + helper invocation

**Execution Phase Steps:**
1. Bash script activates appropriate environment
2. Helper script invoked with `--config` flag
3. Config JSON loaded
4. Data sources resolved (DataStreams from JSON, tables from CSV)
5. Operations executed in sequence
6. Outputs written (PNG, PSE, CSV)
7. Completion marker created

Sources: [biopipelines/pymol.py:659-691](), [biopipelines/plot.py:533-563](), [HelpScripts/pipe_plot.py:740-770]()

---

## Environment Requirements

| Tool | Environment | Key Dependencies | Installation |
|------|-------------|-----------------|--------------|
| **PyMOL** | `ProteinEnv` (conda)<br/>or `pip` (Colab) | `pymol-open-source` | `PyMOL.install()`<br/>or pip mode auto-installs |
| **Plot** | `biopipelines` | `matplotlib`<br/>`seaborn`<br/>`pandas`<br/>`numpy` | No installation needed<br/>(uses biopipelines env) |

**Environment Activation:**
- PyMOL uses [biopipelines/base_config.py:227-281]() `activate_environment()` method
- Plot uses biopipelines environment (already activated for framework)
- Pip mode (Colab/Jupyter): No environment activation, direct `python` invocation

Sources: [biopipelines/pymol.py:66-93](), [biopipelines/plot.py:90-95]()

## Integration with Pipeline

Visualization tools integrate seamlessly with other BioPipelines tools:

```python
from biopipelines import Pipeline, Resources
from biopipelines.boltz2 import Boltz2
from biopipelines.panda import Panda
from biopipelines.plot import Plot
from biopipelines.pymol import PyMOL

with Pipeline("visualization_example"):
    Resources(gpu=1, memory="16GB")
    
    # Structure prediction
    predictions = Boltz2(proteins=sequences, ligands="ATP")
    
    # Filter by confidence
    filtered = Panda(
        tables=predictions.tables.confidence,
        operations=[Panda.filter("confidence_score > 0.8")],
        pool=predictions
    )
    
    # Plot confidence distribution
    Plot(
        Plot.Histogram(data=predictions, x="confidence_score", bins=20),
        Plot.Scatter(data=predictions, x="confidence_score", y="affinity", color="source")
    )
    
    # Render top structures
    PyMOL(
        PyMOL.RenderEach(
            structures=filtered,
            orient_selection="resn ATP",
            color_protein="plddt",
            plddt_upper=1
        )
    )
```

**Key Integration Points:**
1. **Data Flow**: Tools accept `StandardizedOutput` from any upstream tool
2. **Table References**: Can reference table columns for per-ID selections/grouping
3. **Provenance**: Output IDs preserve provenance from input sources
4. **Pooling**: Visualization filters can use `pool` parameter to copy matching files

Sources: [biopipelines/pymol.py:49-61](), [biopipelines/plot.py:49-85]()

# Page: Major Workflows

# Major Workflows

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [ExamplePipelines/boltz2.py](ExamplePipelines/boltz2.py)
- [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen.py](HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen.py)
- [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen_import.py](HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen_import.py)
- [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen_merge.py](HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen_merge.py)

</details>



This page provides an overview of complex multi-tool workflows in BioPipelines that require orchestrated pre-processing, execution, and post-processing steps. These workflows involve multiple helper scripts, specialized file formats, and coordination between tools.

**Scope**: This page covers the general architecture and patterns of major workflows. For detailed implementation guides, see the child pages: [Boltz2 Workflow](#6.1), [BoltzGen Workflow](#6.2), [RFdiffusion3 Workflow](#6.3), and [MMseqs2 Distributed MSA Generation](#6.4).

For simple single-tool usage patterns, see [Tool Categories](#5). For the helper script architecture that enables these workflows, see [Helper Script Architecture](#7.1).

---

## What Are Major Workflows?

Major workflows are multi-step processes that combine BioPipelines tools with specialized helper scripts to accomplish complex bioinformatics tasks. Unlike simple tools like `PDB()` or `Sequence()` that operate independently, major workflows require:

1. **Pre-processing**: Format conversion, structure preparation, configuration generation
2. **Main execution**: Running the core tool (often an external software package)
3. **Post-processing**: Extracting results, renaming IDs, merging outputs, validation

These workflows are necessary when integrating external tools that have specific filesystem requirements, custom output formats, or need multiple execution stages.

**Key Characteristics**:
- Multiple helper scripts coordinated by a single tool class
- Specialized file format requirements (CIF, NPZ, YAML configs)
- Multi-stage execution (import → design → analysis → merge)
- ID mapping and provenance tracking across stages
- Complex combinatorics with Bundle/Each operators

Sources: [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen_import.py:1-22](), [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen_merge.py:1-24](), [ExamplePipelines/boltz2.py:1-251]()

---

## Simple vs. Complex Workflows

The following diagram illustrates the difference between simple single-tool operations and complex multi-step workflows:

**Diagram: Workflow Complexity Spectrum**

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Simple["Simple Single-Tool Workflow"]
        S_User["User Code:<br/>pdb = PDB('1AKI')"]
        S_Tool["Tool Class:<br/>PDB"]
        S_Script["Helper Script:<br/>pipe_pdb.py"]
        S_Output["StandardizedOutput:<br/>.streams.structures"]
        
        S_User --> S_Tool
        S_Tool --> S_Script
        S_Script --> S_Output
    end
    
    subgraph Complex["Complex Multi-Stage Workflow"]
        C_User["User Code:<br/>boltzgen = BoltzGen(...)"]
        C_Tool["Tool Class:<br/>BoltzGen"]
        
        subgraph Stage1["Pre-processing Stage"]
            C_Import["pipe_boltzgen_import.py<br/>Format conversion<br/>Chain reassignment<br/>NPZ generation"]
        end
        
        subgraph Stage2["Main Execution Stage"]
            C_Design["BoltzGen binary<br/>Design generation<br/>Inverse folding"]
        end
        
        subgraph Stage3["Post-processing Stage"]
            C_Post["pipe_boltzgen.py<br/>Sequence extraction<br/>Metrics processing"]
            C_Merge["pipe_boltzgen_merge.py<br/>Multi-run merging<br/>ID renaming"]
        end
        
        C_Output["StandardizedOutput:<br/>.streams.structures<br/>.streams.sequences<br/>.tables.metrics"]
        
        C_User --> C_Tool
        C_Tool --> C_Import
        C_Import --> C_Design
        C_Design --> C_Post
        C_Post --> C_Merge
        C_Merge --> C_Output
    end
    
    style S_Tool fill:#ffe1e1
    style C_Tool fill:#ffe1e1
    style C_Import fill:#e1f5ff
    style C_Post fill:#e1f5ff
    style C_Merge fill:#e1f5ff
```

Sources: [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen_import.py:6-22](), [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen.py:6-14](), [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen_merge.py:6-24]()

---

## Helper Script Orchestration Pattern

Major workflows follow a consistent pattern where a single tool class (inheriting from `BaseConfig`) orchestrates multiple helper scripts. The tool class is responsible for generating bash scripts that call helper scripts in the correct order with appropriate arguments.

**Diagram: Helper Script Orchestration Architecture**

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph UserLayer["User Layer (Python)"]
        UserCode["Pipeline Script<br/>with BoltzGen(...) call"]
    end
    
    subgraph ToolLayer["Tool Layer (Python - Configuration Phase)"]
        ToolClass["BoltzGen class<br/>inherits BaseConfig"]
        
        ValidateParams["validate_params()<br/>Check input validity"]
        ConfigureInputs["configure_inputs()<br/>Predict file paths"]
        GenerateScript["generate_script()<br/>Write bash orchestrator"]
        GetOutputFiles["get_output_files()<br/>Register outputs"]
        
        ToolClass --> ValidateParams
        ToolClass --> ConfigureInputs
        ToolClass --> GenerateScript
        ToolClass --> GetOutputFiles
    end
    
    subgraph ScriptLayer["Script Layer (Bash - Execution Phase)"]
        BashOrchestrator["Generated bash script<br/>boltzgen_run.sh"]
        
        StepImport["Step 1: Import<br/>pipe_boltzgen_import.py<br/>--structures --output<br/>--mode --sequences"]
        
        StepDesign["Step 2: Design<br/>BoltzGen binary<br/>--input --output<br/>--budget --steps"]
        
        StepPost["Step 3: Postprocess<br/>pipe_boltzgen.py<br/>--output_folder --budget<br/>--extract_sequences"]
        
        StepMerge["Step 4: Merge (optional)<br/>pipe_boltzgen_merge.py<br/>--sources --output<br/>--id_template"]
        
        BashOrchestrator --> StepImport
        StepImport --> StepDesign
        StepDesign --> StepPost
        StepPost --> StepMerge
    end
    
    subgraph OutputLayer["Output Layer"]
        Structures["structures.csv<br/>sequences.csv<br/>metrics.csv"]
        DataStream["DataStream objects<br/>.streams.structures<br/>.streams.sequences"]
        TableInfo["TableInfo objects<br/>.tables.metrics"]
    end
    
    UserCode --> ToolClass
    GenerateScript --> BashOrchestrator
    StepMerge --> Structures
    Structures --> DataStream
    Structures --> TableInfo
    
    style ToolClass fill:#ffe1e1
    style BashOrchestrator fill:#fff4e1
    style StepImport fill:#e1f5ff
    style StepPost fill:#e1f5ff
    style StepMerge fill:#e1f5ff
```

Sources: [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen_import.py:942-1060](), [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen.py:231-325](), [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen_merge.py:415-495]()

---

## Pre-Processing: Format Conversion and Preparation

Pre-processing helper scripts convert external data into the format required by downstream tools. This often involves:

- **Structure format conversion**: PDB → CIF with specific mmCIF fields
- **Chain reassignment**: Standardizing chain IDs (protein=A, ligand=B)
- **Metadata generation**: Creating NPZ files with per-token annotations
- **Configuration files**: Generating YAML files with design specifications

**Example: BoltzGen Import Process**

The `pipe_boltzgen_import.py` script demonstrates a comprehensive pre-processing workflow:

```mermaid
graph LR
    Input["External PDB files<br/>from RFdiffusion etc."]
    
    ReadPDB["read_pdb()<br/>Parse ATOM/HETATM records<br/>Organize by chain/residue"]
    
    Reassign["convert_and_reassign_chains()<br/>Longest chain → protein (A)<br/>Non-AA residues → ligand (B)<br/>Apply sequence (inverse folding)"]
    
    WriteCIF["write_cif()<br/>Generate mmCIF format<br/>entity_poly, atom_site loops<br/>pLDDT metadata"]
    
    GenerateNPZ["generate_npz_metadata()<br/>design_mask arrays<br/>ss_type, binding_type<br/>token_resolved_mask"]
    
    DesignSpec["generate_design_spec()<br/>YAML with entity definitions<br/>Binder length spec<br/>Ligand SMILES/CCD"]
    
    Output["BoltzGen-compatible:<br/>design_spec_N.cif<br/>design_spec_N.npz<br/>design_spec.yaml"]
    
    Input --> ReadPDB
    ReadPDB --> Reassign
    Reassign --> WriteCIF
    Reassign --> GenerateNPZ
    Reassign --> DesignSpec
    WriteCIF --> Output
    GenerateNPZ --> Output
    DesignSpec --> Output
    
    style ReadPDB fill:#e1f5ff
    style Reassign fill:#e1f5ff
    style WriteCIF fill:#e1f5ff
    style GenerateNPZ fill:#e1f5ff
    style DesignSpec fill:#e1f5ff
```

**Key Implementation Details**:

| Function | Purpose | Key Operations |
|----------|---------|----------------|
| `read_pdb()` | Parse PDB manually | Extract ATOM/HETATM records into chain/residue structure |
| `convert_and_reassign_chains()` | Standardize structure | Identify protein (longest chain), separate ligand, apply sequence mutations |
| `write_cif()` | Generate mmCIF | Create entity loops, atom_site records, pLDDT metadata |
| `generate_npz_metadata()` | Create NPZ arrays | design_mask (1.0=protein, 0.0=ligand), ss_type, binding_type |
| `generate_design_spec()` | Create YAML config | Entity definitions with binder length and ligand info |

The CIF format is used instead of PDB because:
1. CIF allows longer residue names (e.g., `LIG1`) vs. PDB's 3-character limit
2. BoltzGen's `parse_mmcif` accepts the `mols` dictionary for ligand resolution, while `parse_pdb` does not

Sources: [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen_import.py:130-146](), [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen_import.py:355-522](), [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen_import.py:148-353](), [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen_import.py:717-784](), [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen_import.py:663-714]()

## Post-Processing: Extraction and Validation

Post-processing scripts extract useful data from tool outputs and convert them to BioPipelines' standardized formats. This includes:

- **Sequence extraction**: Reading protein sequences from structure files
- **Metrics processing**: Converting tool-specific CSV formats to standard tables
- **Validation**: Checking that expected outputs were generated
- **ID mapping**: Creating correspondence between structure IDs and sequences

**Example: BoltzGen Postprocessing**

```mermaid
graph TB
    Input["BoltzGen output:<br/>final_ranked_designs/<br/>final_N_designs/*.cif<br/>final_designs_metrics_N.csv"]
    
    CollectStructs["collect_and_process_structures()<br/>Find all .cif/.pdb files<br/>Sort for consistent ordering"]
    
    ExtractSeq["extract_sequence_from_structure()<br/>BioPython MMCIFParser/PDBParser<br/>Extract first chain sequence<br/>3-letter → 1-letter conversion"]
    
    CreateSeqDF["Create sequences.csv<br/>id, sequence columns<br/>One row per structure"]
    
    CreateStructDF["Create structures.csv<br/>id, pdb columns<br/>Absolute file paths"]
    
    ProcessMetrics["process_metrics()<br/>Validate metrics CSV<br/>Check for 'id' column"]
    
    Validate["validate_outputs()<br/>Check final_designs_folder exists<br/>Check metrics CSV exists<br/>Verify sequences.csv created"]
    
    Output["BioPipelines-compatible:<br/>sequences.csv<br/>structures.csv<br/>final_structures.txt"]
    
    Input --> CollectStructs
    CollectStructs --> ExtractSeq
    ExtractSeq --> CreateSeqDF
    ExtractSeq --> CreateStructDF
    Input --> ProcessMetrics
    CreateSeqDF --> Validate
    CreateStructDF --> Validate
    ProcessMetrics --> Validate
    Validate --> Output
    
    style CollectStructs fill:#e1f5ff
    style ExtractSeq fill:#e1f5ff
    style ProcessMetrics fill:#e1f5ff
    style Validate fill:#e1f5ff
```

Sources: [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen.py:72-149](), [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen.py:23-70](), [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen.py:151-188](), [HelpScripts/pipe_boltzgen.py:190-228]()
